attributes.name: UI Design Contract Workflow
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Generates a binding, checker-verified UI specification (`{phase}-UI-SPEC.md`) for phases with significant frontend work. Orchestrates UI researcher and checker agents through a four-stage pipeline, enforcing React + shadcn/Tailwind design system consistency before any frontend implementation begins.

## Architecture
**Four-stage pipeline: `validate` → `research` → `verify` → `done`**

- **`validate`**: Brand reference (`ui-brand.md`) and workflow gate requirements loaded; React + shadcn/Tailwind stack constraints established. Gates must clear before research begins.
- **`research`**: UI researcher generates an initial spec grounded in existing codebase component patterns and the locked `{phase}-CONTEXT.md`. Spec must be anchored to real shadcn registry components, not hypothetical ones.
- **`verify`**: Checker evaluates all **6 mandatory dimensions**: typography, copywriting, visuals, color, spacing, registry safety. Any **blocking issue** routes back to `research` for a revision loop; flag warnings also require resolution before advancing.
- **`done`**: All 6 dimensions cleared; spec written to the phase directory with `status: approved` frontmatter.

**Revision loop behavior**: Blocking issues force re-entry to `research`. The most common first-pass failure is typography inconsistency (too many distinct font size variants), resolved by consolidating to exactly **4 distinct font sizes**. Copywriting and visuals flag warnings frequently accompany the first pass and must also clear before `done`.

## Key Files
- `~/.claude/get-shit-done/ui-brand.md` — brand reference and design system constraints; loaded at `validate` stage
- `.planning/phases/{phase}-{slug}/{phase}-UI-SPEC.md` — output artifact with `status: approved` frontmatter
  - Example: `.planning/phases/74-performance-dashboard-reports/74-UI-SPEC.md`

## Usage
Invoked after `gsd-discuss-phase` completes (requires a locked `{phase}-CONTEXT.md`) and before `gsd-plan-phase` or any frontend implementation. The `status: approved` frontmatter in the spec is the readiness gate consumed by downstream implementors and subagents during `gsd-execute-phase`.

## Troubleshooting
- **Blocking issue on first verify pass**: Consolidate font sizes to exactly 4 distinct sizes; this resolves the most common typography failure.
- **Copywriting or visuals warnings not clearing**: Non-blocking individually but must all clear before `done`; re-enter `research` with targeted revision instructions for flagged dimensions.
- **Spec references non-existent components**: Re-prompt researcher to use only shadcn registry components confirmed present in the codebase.
- **Gate stuck at `validate`**: Confirm `ui-brand.md` is readable and `{phase}-CONTEXT.md` exists and is locked (not draft status).
- **Verify dimension count mismatch**: Exactly 6 dimensions are evaluated; if checker reports fewer, the workflow is incomplete and should not advance to `done`.

attributes.name: gsd-execute-phase Skill
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Wave-based execution orchestrator for locked, fully-verified GSD phases. Loads per-phase plan artifacts, constructs a dependency-ordered DAG, dispatches isolated sub-agents per plan with fresh context budgets, and enforces pre-execution integrity gates before any sub-agent is spawned. A mandatory pre-execution context reset prevents planning-session state from polluting execution.

## Architecture
**Invocation:** `/gsd-execute-phase [phase] [--wave N] [--gaps-only] [--interactive]`

**Flag parsing — literal token matching only:**
| Flag | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `--wave N` | Execute only wave N |
| `--gaps-only` | Execute only plans with `gap_closure: true` in frontmatter; all others skipped |
| `--interactive` | Interactive execution mode |
| *(no flags)* | Full-phase execution |

Abbreviations (`--gap`) and `=` syntax (`--wave=2`) are silently unrecognized and fall back to full-phase execution.

**Execution sequence (all steps complete before any sub-agent is spawned):**
1. Mandatory pre-execution context reset — clears planning-session state
2. Load per-phase plan artifacts from disk
3. Construct dependency-ordered DAG
4. Pre-execution integrity gate enforcement (see GSD Plan Verification Gate insight)
5. Dispatch isolated sub-agents per plan, each with a fresh context budget

## Key Files
- Per-phase plan artifact files (disk) — loaded at step 2; must be current and committed before invocation
- `gsd-plan-checker` integrity gate — enforced at step 4

## Usage
Invoked by operator after `gsd-plan-phase` output passes the plan verification gate. Wave-scoped invocations (`--wave N`) re-enter mid-phase; `--gaps-only` targets only gap-closure plans. Sub-agents are fully isolated per plan — no shared state between concurrent dispatches.

## Troubleshooting
- **`--gaps-only` silently ignored**: Confirm exact spelling (`--gaps-only`, not `--gap` or `--gaps`); abbreviations fall back to full-phase execution without warning.
- **`--wave=2` not recognized**: Use space-separated form `--wave 2`; `=` syntax is unrecognized.
- **Planning state contaminating execution**: Confirm mandatory context reset completed before sub-agents were spawned. If contamination is suspected, abort, reset context manually, and re-invoke.
- **Sub-agent dispatched with stale plan**: Verify plan artifacts on disk are current before invocation; re-run `gsd-plan-phase` if plans were modified post-gate.

attributes.name: gsd-plan-phase Skill
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Converts a locked `{phase}-CONTEXT.md` into a verified, executable plan set. Orchestrates `gsd-phase-researcher`, `gsd-planner` (opus-class), and `gsd-plan-checker` (sonnet-class) through a configurable gate system and an iterative Plan → Verify correction loop until all plans pass integrity gates or max iterations are exhausted. Does not execute plans — execution is the exclusive responsibility of `gsd-execute-phase`.

## Architecture
- **Invocation**: `/gsd-plan-phase [phase] [flags]`
- **Workflow file**: `~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/plan-phase.md` — loaded in full before any action; governs all behavior, alongside UI guidance from `ui-brand.md` when the phase involves UI work.
- **Core loop**: `research → plan → verify → done`; correction loop iterates Plan → Verify until `gsd-plan-checker` returns pass or max iterations is reached.
- **Sub-agents**: `gsd-phase-researcher` (research stage, conditionally spawned), `gsd-planner` (opus-class, plan generation), `gsd-plan-checker` (sonnet-class, integrity verification).
- **Research control flags**: `--research` (force research), `--view` (view existing research), `--skip-research` (bypass research stage entirely).
- **Planner input sources**: discuss-phase context (default), `--prd` (external PRD ingestion), `--ingest` (ADR ingestion).
- **Planning mode flags**: `--gaps` (gap-closure planning), `--mvp` (MVP vertical slicing), `--reviews` (incorporate cross-AI review feedback).

## Key Files
- `~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/plan-phase.md` — canonical workflow definition
- `ui-brand.md` — UI guideline reference consulted for UI-scoped phases
- `{phase}-CONTEXT.md` — required locked input artifact

## Usage
Run by the `claude` or `copilot` agent after discuss-phase produces a locked `{phase}-CONTEXT.md`; output plan set is the mandatory input to `gsd-execute-phase` after passing the plan verification gate.

## Troubleshooting
- If no plans are produced, confirm `{phase}-CONTEXT.md` exists and is locked — plan-phase will not proceed on an unresolved discuss-phase.
- If the correction loop never terminates, check `gsd-plan-checker` output for recurring integrity failures (source coverage, file-overlap) rather than assuming max-iteration exhaustion is a bug.
- Flag typos (e.g. `--wave=2` instead of `--wave 2`) are silently unrecognized elsewhere in GSD tooling — verify exact flag syntax matches documented forms.

attributes.name: Performance Dashboard — Experiment Scoring UI
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Renders multi-turn experiment run data — 5-dimension rubric scores, per-turn timelines with reasoning-step sub-bands, and corrected-wins override state — for human review and correction. Acts as the visual layer over the experiment store's `Run`/`Score`/`Outcome` data model. Includes an operator toggle to surface quarantined (smoke-test) runs that are hidden by default.

## Architecture
**State management (`performanceSlice.ts`):**
- Redux slice owning all performance scoring state; applies optimistic updates for override edits before the lagging km-core re-fetch arrives.
- **Staleness hazard**: km-core's debounced JSON export can return a pre-override snapshot on re-fetch; the optimistic update patches local state immediately on save to prevent stale values from overwriting the UI.
- **Model facet filtering** operates on the multi-valued union of `canonical_model` and `background_models` (ATTR-02 fields); the legacy `run.model` field is **not** used for filtering.

**Run visibility and quarantine filtering:**
- The `:8080` experiment API applies a pending/trivial run quarantine filter by default; smoke runs are suppressed in the default endpoint view.
- `readRuns(store, {includePending:true})` bypasses the quarantine and returns all runs, including smoke runs.
- The store export JSON is the authoritative ground truth — if it contains all expected `task_id` entries, a count discrepancy in the dashboard is caused by the endpoint filter, not a persistence failure.
- Fix options: adjust the executor's filter criteria, or enable `includePending:true` in the dashboard config.

## Key Files
- `performanceSlice.ts` — Redux slice; optimistic override updates, model facet filtering, re-fetch debounce handling
- Experiment API at `:8080` — applies quarantine filter by default; `readRuns(store, {includePending:true})` bypasses it
- Store export JSON — authoritative `task_id` manifest; verify here first when diagnosing run-count discrepancies

## Usage
Used by the performance dashboard UI for human review and correction of experiment run scoring. The operator toggle for quarantined runs allows surfacing smoke-test runs suppressed in the default view. `readRuns` with `includePending:true` is the programmatic path to the full unfiltered run list.

## Troubleshooting
- **Run count lower than expected (e.g., 12 of 15):** First confirm the store export JSON contains all expected `task_id` entries. If it does, the shortfall is the endpoint quarantine filter suppressing pending/trivial runs — enable `includePending:true` or adjust filter criteria in the executor.
- **Stale scores after override:** km-core's debounced JSON export may return a pre-override snapshot; the optimistic update in `performanceSlice.ts` guards against UI regression, but a full page reload may transiently show stale values.
- **Smoke runs missing from dashboard:** Confirm the operator toggle is enabled; if still absent, check whether the executor is labeling them as pending/trivial and whether `includePending` is wired through the dashboard config.

attributes.name: gsd-discuss-phase Skill
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Post-phase-close security gate that extracts all declared STRIDE threats from sub-plan artifacts, dispatches `gsd-security-auditor` to verify every mitigation is present in implementation code (not rubber-stamped), and commits `{phase}-SECURITY.md` when the SECURED ✓ verdict clears. Runs as a fully standalone pass — separate from main execution, code review, and the Phase Close-Out Protocol.

## Architecture
- **Entrypoint**: `/gsd-secure-phase [phase]`
- **Workflow file**: `~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/secure-phase.md` — loaded in full before any action; governs all audit behavior.
- **Invocation timing**: Surfaced as "outstanding" at step 6 of the Phase Close-Out Protocol; must **not** be triggered during close-out — requires explicit operator dispatch only after step 6 fully completes.
- **Two-stage execution (strict ordering)**:
  1. *Stage 1* — Load `secure-phase.md`; verify gate-preserving logic is ready. No artifacts produced, no files modified.
  2. *Stage 2* — Extract STRIDE threats from sub-plan artifacts; dispatch `gsd-security-auditor` sub-agent; verify mitigations exist in implementation code; commit `{phase}-SECURITY.md` on SECURED ✓ verdict.

## Key Files
- `~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/secure-phase.md` — governing workflow file; must be loaded before any audit action
- `{phase}-SECURITY.md` — output artifact committed only on SECURED ✓ verdict

## Usage
Invoked explicitly by the operator via `/gsd-secure-phase [phase]` after Phase Close-Out Protocol step 6 completes. Never auto-triggered. The `gsd-security-auditor` sub-agent performs mitigation verification; this workflow orchestrates it.

## Troubleshooting
- **Invoked during close-out (not after)**: Invalid — abort and re-invoke only after step 6 of Phase Close-Out Protocol fully completes.
- **`secure-phase.md` not found**: Verify `~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/` directory exists and the file is present before invoking.
- **STRIDE threats not extracted**: Confirm sub-plan artifacts for the target phase exist and contain STRIDE threat declarations.
- **Audit rubber-stamps mitigations without deep verification**: Check `gsd-security-auditor` sub-agent prompt and injected toolset for verification depth.

- **`secure-phase.md` not found**: Verify `~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/` directory exists and the file is present before invoking.

attributes.name: Performance Dashboard — Experiment Controls and Stop Routing
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Browser UI controls that bound measurement spans for experiment performance reporting. The Stop action triggers the full experiment close pipeline (token aggregation → LLM judge → `Run`/`Score` write). Routes entirely through `vkb-server`'s existing experiment endpoints — no separate server infrastructure required.

## Architecture
- **Start**: `measurement-start.mjs` stamps a `task_id` with format `exp-{context}-{condition}-{model}-{run}` (e.g., `exp-dash-start-control-claude-opus-4-8`).
- **Stop**: `measurement-stop.mjs` orchestrates a sequential pipeline: token aggregation → six scoring heuristics → LLM judge → `Run`/`Score` write.
- Re-runs with varied parameters are comparable across run series via a shared `task_hash`.
- **Two-store boundary**:
  - Experiment metadata: dedicated LevelDB store.
  - Token/cost data: `token-usage.db` (SQLite).
- Dashboard start/stop routes through `vkb-server`'s existing experiment endpoints; no additional server process needed.

## Key Files
- `measurement-start.mjs` — stamps `task_id` at experiment start.
- `measurement-stop.mjs` — orchestrates the stop pipeline (aggregation → scoring → write).
- `token-usage.db` — SQLite store for per-run token and cost data.
- `vkb-server` — hosts experiment API endpoints; routes dashboard start/stop calls.

## Usage
- Developer initiates and terminates experiments from the browser UI; start/stop buttons call `vkb-server` experiment endpoints.
- Each completed run produces a `Run` record and `Score` records in the LevelDB experiment store.
- `task_hash` enables cross-run comparison across varied parameter sets within a run series.

## Troubleshooting
- **Stop pipeline stalls**: the pipeline is sequential — token aggregation must complete before scoring; LLM judge timeout will block the `Run`/`Score` write. Check `measurement-stop.mjs` step-by-step logs.
- **Run records not appearing in dashboard**: verify `vkb-server` experiment endpoints are reachable and the LevelDB store is accessible.
- **Scores inconsistent across re-runs**: LLM judge output is non-deterministic; the six heuristic scoring steps are deterministic and should be stable — isolate which score component is varying to determine whether it is the judge or a heuristic.

attributes.name: Measurement Orchestrator
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Orchestrates the full measurement-stop close pipeline: token aggregation, six flat deterministic heuristics, freeform goal sentence derivation, idempotent route node writes, and LLM judge scoring. Materializes per-run routing decisions, outcome metrics, and scores into the experiment store on `/gsd close`. Exposes two idempotent recompute CLIs for retroactive correction without touching live data. All stop/close requests route exclusively through `vkb-server`'s `/api/experiments/*` endpoints.

## Architecture
Four integrated subsystems wired through `measurement-stop.mjs`:

**Route node writes (idempotent):**
- `/gsd close` writes exactly one Route node per run with a `tookRoute` edge
- Idempotency guard checks for an existing Route node before writing — re-running close never produces a duplicate

**Six flat heuristics** (deterministic, zero-LLM, stored on the `Run` entity):
- `loopCount` — number of repeated execution loops
- Five additional heuristics derived from run telemetry

**Date sorting (defensive):**
- Numeric date comparisons in run ordering use **NaN-last handling** — malformed or unparseable date values sort after all valid dates; prevents undefined ordering or front-of-list pollution from bad inputs

**LLM judge scoring:**
- Freeform goal sentence is derived before the LLM scoring step
- Scores stored on the experiment entity alongside all heuristic fields

## Key Files
- `scripts/measurement-stop.mjs` — full close pipeline: token aggregation, heuristics, NaN-last date sort, route writes, LLM scoring
- `vkb-server/routes/experiments.js` — HTTP endpoints `/api/experiments/*` receiving all close/stop requests

## Usage
Triggered by `/gsd close` during an active experiment run. Two idempotent recompute CLIs allow retroactive correction of stored metrics without altering live run data. All requests must route through `vkb-server`; direct DB writes bypass idempotency guards.

## Troubleshooting
- **Duplicate Route nodes**: idempotency guard was bypassed (e.g., direct DB write); use the recompute CLI to reconcile
- **Run ordering anomalies**: NaN-last guard in date sort prevents malformed values from corrupting order; if ordering appears wrong, inspect run store for non-ISO or unparseable date strings
- **Partial runs (heuristics written, no score)**: LLM scoring is the final stage; an LLM call failure after heuristic materialization leaves this state; recompute CLI can rerun scoring only

attributes.name: Phase 75 — Measurement Attribution and ETM Recapture Components
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Builds the foundational `lib/repro/` modules and snapshot/restore rig for the GSD reproducibility system: deterministic LLM fixture recording/replay, environment and git-state capture, KB snapshot assembly, and isolated per-variant workspace restore. These artifacts underpin the REPRO-01/REPRO-02 system and are direct dependencies for Phase 77's per-variant snapshot restore step.

## Architecture
Seven plans (67-01 through 67-07) across 3 waves. Waves 1–2 complete; Wave 3 plans (67-02, 67-05, 67-07) partially resolved — snapshot/restore rig confirmed complete and callable.

**Wave 1 — Fixture primitives and environment capture (Plans 67-01, 67-03):**
- `lib/repro/fixtures/match-key.mjs` — single deterministic match-key design for fixture lookup
- `lib/repro/fixtures/llm-record.mjs` — records LLM request/response pairs as JSONL fixtures
- `lib/repro/fixtures/llm-replay.mjs` — replays fixtures; honest hard-fail on cache miss (no silent fallback to live LLM)

## Key Files
- `lib/repro/fixtures/match-key.mjs` — deterministic fixture lookup key generation
- `lib/repro/fixtures/llm-record.mjs` — LLM fixture recorder (JSONL output)
- `lib/repro/fixtures/llm-replay.mjs` — LLM fixture replayer (hard-fail on cache miss)
- `lib/repro/` — full reproducibility module tree

## Usage
- Used by the REPRO-01/REPRO-02 system for deterministic LLM call replay in reproducibility testing.
- Phase 77 depends on the Wave 3 snapshot/restore rig being callable before proceeding.
- Replay mode requires all fixtures to be pre-recorded; no silent fallback to live LLM calls exists.

## Troubleshooting
- Fixture replay failure on cache miss is intentional hard-fail behavior — ensure all required fixtures are recorded in record mode before switching to replay mode.
- If Wave 3 plan status is uncertain, verify snapshot/restore rig is callable (not just present) before initiating Phase 77 dependencies.

attributes.name: ETM Mid-Turn Progress Observations — Token-Delta Trigger
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Fires an in-progress observation snapshot during long-running turns when the accumulated output-token delta crosses a configurable threshold (default: 30,000 tokens). Ensures partial work is persisted to km-core mid-turn, providing durability and intermediate visibility without waiting for turn completion. Produces zero overhead on short turns that never cross the threshold.

## Architecture
**Threshold calibration:**
- 30k tokens empirically derived from observed session output volumes (~12k–135k tokens per turn)
- Yields ~3–4 snapshots on the heaviest turns at ~12–15 minute intervals
- 20k explicitly rejected as too granular (~6 snapshots on the heaviest turns)

**Runtime configuration:**
- `ETM_PROGRESS_TOKEN_DELTA` environment variable overrides the 30k default for per-deployment tuning without code changes

**Trigger mechanism:**
- `_progressFiredTokens` accumulator tracks output tokens scoped per prompt-set during live polling
- When the delta crosses the threshold, fires a dedup-keyed `kind:'progress'` observation without closing the turn, then resets the accumulator
- Mirrors the existing mid-set fire boundary pattern; does not affect turn narrative integrity

**Separation of concerns:**
- Mid-turn progress observations are distinct from the final per-turn observation
- `kind:'progress'` observations are explicitly exempted from semantic dedup in `ObservationWriter._isSemanticallyDuplicate`, preventing in-progress snapshots from being collapsed into finals
- Progress records may later be promoted to finals by `ObservationWriter._promoteProgressSnapshot` via content-hash matching if a matching final arrives

## Key Files
- ETM source file (exact path not confirmed) — hosts `_progressFiredTokens` accumulator and token-delta trigger logic
- `ObservationWriter.js` — handles `kind:'progress'` dedup exemption and snapshot promotion

## Usage
- Active during any turn where output volume exceeds the threshold (~30k tokens); silent on short turns
- Consumed by the km-core observation store; records tagged `kind:'progress'` are candidates for snapshot promotion
- Threshold configurable at deployment time via `ETM_PROGRESS_TOKEN_DELTA` without code changes

## Troubleshooting
- **No mid-turn snapshots appearing**: Confirm output volume for the turn exceeds `ETM_PROGRESS_TOKEN_DELTA` (default 30k); verify the accumulator is reset correctly between prompt-sets
- **Too many snapshots on all turns**: Threshold is too low — raise `ETM_PROGRESS_TOKEN_DELTA`; note that 20k was judged too granular for typical sessions
- **Progress records incorrectly deduped away**: Verify that the `kind:'progress'` exemption in `ObservationWriter._isSemanticallyDuplicate` is active and that the `kind` field is being set correctly at the ETM fire path
- **Progress records not promoted to finals**: Check `ObservationWriter._promoteProgressSnapshot` — confirm content-hash computation is consistent between the in-progress and final fire paths

attributes.name: ETM Fire Cursor — State Persistence and Deduplication
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Tracks which prompt-set exchanges have already been observation-fired, enabling deduplication across ETM restarts, mid-turn progress fires, and long-turn force-flush paths. An incorrect cursor key, lost cursor state, or unauthorized cursor advancement silently produces duplicate observation records or permanently blocks all future fires — none of these failure modes produce a crash or an explicit error signal.

## Architecture
**Cursor fields (both persisted to the ETM state file):**
- `_lastFiredExchangeUuid` — monotonically advancing pointer into the processed exchange sequence; shared by mid-turn progress fires and final completion fires; written after each successful fire; loaded at ETM construction time so restarts resume from the correct position without re-firing
- `_progressFiredTokens` — accumulated token delta per prompt-set; prevents re-firing of progress checkpoints after a restart resets in-memory state

**Cursor key — critical invariant:**
- Must be keyed on the **immutable exchange start ID** (`exchangeStartId`) rather than any mutable or turn-scoped field; a mutable key causes the deduplication logic to re-fire already-processed exchanges after an in-turn edit

**Silent cursor advancement by failed singleton instances:**
- When the singleton guard rejects a respawned ETM instance, that instance may advance the cursor before exiting; this marks exchanges as processed in the cursor state without emitting observations, producing a permanent silent gap
- Detection: cursor `_lastFiredExchangeUuid` is positioned past exchanges that have no corresponding rows in `observations.db`
- Root cause: singleton deadlock (see "ETM Singleton Arbitration and Reclaim"); fix involves clearing the stale holder, then resetting the cursor to the last confirmed observation UUID if gap is unacceptable

## Key Files
- `~/Agentic/coding/scripts/enhanced-transcript-monitor.js` — cursor fields defined and loaded at construction; written after each successful fire; resubmission driver consumes `_lastFiredExchangeUuid` to skip already-fired exchanges
- ETM state file — persisted cursor storage; path determined by project root
- `singleton-reclaim.mjs` — prevents the respawn-storm scenario that enables unauthorized cursor advancement

## Usage
The cursor is entirely internal to ETM; no external component writes to it. The resubmission driver uses `_lastFiredExchangeUuid` to skip already-fired exchanges on infinite-retry cycles. The cursor is the sole source of truth for which exchanges are considered processed — any divergence from `observations.db` row count indicates a gap.

## Troubleshooting
- **Duplicate observations after restart**: Cursor state file lost or cursor key changed to a mutable field; audit the key used in the deduplication check
- **All future fires blocked**: Cursor advanced to a UUID absent from the exchange sequence; correct by resetting `_lastFiredExchangeUuid` in the state file to the last valid observation UUID
- **Silent observation gap (cursor advanced, no matching DB rows)**: Failed singleton guard instances advanced the cursor; kill all ETM processes simultaneously, verify row count in `observations.db` against expected exchange count, and manually reset the cursor if the gap must be filled
- **Verify cursor integrity**: Inspect the ETM state file directly; compare `_lastFiredExchangeUuid` against the exchange UUID on the latest `observations.db` row — they should match or the cursor should be one exchange ahead (in-flight)

attributes.name: Cold-Store Exporter — Write Lag
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Persists km-core observations from the live LevelDB graph to the durable JSON cold-store used by downstream consumers (dashboard, insight consolidation) and as the authoritative hydration source on km-core restart. Write lag causes the cold-store snapshot to fall behind the live km-core count, leaving recent observations — including `kind:'progress'` snapshots — inaccessible to any consumer reading from the cold-store JSON.

## Architecture
- **Two persistence layers**: km-core live graph (LevelDB / in-memory, live query target) and cold-store JSON at `.data/exports/knowledge-export/general.json` (durable snapshot; also read by `lib/km-core/src/store/persistence.ts` at restart — see "km-core Knowledge Graph Hydration" insight).
- The exporter runs after observation writes complete; its job is to flush new records from the live graph into the cold-store JSON.
- **Known downstream symptom**: `kind:'progress'` snapshots confirmed written to km-core may not appear in dashboard views if the exporter is lagging; this is a separate failure from the write path itself.
- **Suspected failure modes** (under active investigation): (a) exporter merge/dedup logic incorrectly treating new records as already-present and skipping them; (b) export trigger not firing after certain write paths (e.g., progress-emitter fire path); (c) slow/blocked I/O delaying the flush.

## Key Files
- `.data/exports/knowledge-export/general.json` — canonical cold-store snapshot; authoritative hydration source
- `lib/km-core/src/store/persistence.ts` — hydration logic; reads cold-store JSON on km-core startup when patched (see "km-core Knowledge Graph Hydration" insight)

## Usage
Runs automatically after observation writes. Output is consumed by the dashboard rendering layer, insight consolidation, and km-core hydration on restart. Lag in this layer does not affect live km-core query results — only consumers reading the cold-store JSON are impacted.

## Troubleshooting
- **Progress snapshots confirmed in km-core but absent from dashboard**: cold-store exporter is lagging; inspect `.data/exports/knowledge-export/general.json` directly for the expected records.
- **Live graph count ahead of cold-store count**: confirm the export trigger fires after the specific write path in question; check for merge/dedup false-positives treating new records as already-exported.
- **Graph collapse on km-core restart**: cold-store is stale and `persistence.ts` is loading stale LevelDB cache; ensure the `persistence.ts` hydration patch (JSON-first preference) is applied to both source and compiled dist artifact.

Runs automatically after observation writes. Output is consumed by the dashboard rendering layer, insight consolidation, and km-core hydration on restart. Lag in this layer does not affect live km-core query results — only consumers reading the cold-store JSON are impacted.

## Troubleshooting
- **Progress snapshots confirmed in km-core but absent from dashboard**: cold-store exporter is lagging; inspect `.data/exports/knowledge-export/general.json` directly for the expected records.
- **Live graph count ahead of cold-store count**: confirm the export trigger fires after the specific write path in question; check for merge/dedup false-positives treating new records as already-exported.
- **Graph collapse on km-core restart**: cold-store is stale and `persistence.ts` is loading stale LevelDB cache; ensure the `persistence.ts` hydration patch (JSON-first preference) is applied to both source and compiled dist artifact.

attributes.name: System Health Dashboard — Dark Mode CSS
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Provides dark-mode rendering compatibility across the system-health-dashboard UI, preventing light-mode color artifacts (white canvases, invisible legend text, bright status banners) when dark mode is active. Implemented as a two-layer system: a global CSS override block plus component-level Tailwind `dark:` variants. A color-token refactor is planned to close the remaining SVG inline-fill gap.

## Architecture
**Layer 1 — Global CSS override** (`system-health-dashboard/src/index.css`):
- A `.dark`-scoped block remaps ~280 hardcoded status utility classes (backgrounds, text, borders) to a consistent dark palette
- Specificity-based targeting — no `!important`; light-mode styles entirely untouched
- Covers core status classes (healthy, warning, error, unknown) plus accent colors: purple, violet, indigo, fuchsia, pink, cyan, teal
- Key semantic fix: "Healthy" banner → green text on dark-green tint background (was white text on light-green)
- Also remaps `fill-slate-*`, `stroke-slate-*`, and `bg-white` utilities to dark-readable values

**Layer 2 — Tailwind `dark:` variants** (graph components):
- `dark:` prefixes on canvas gradient utilities (`from-slate-50 to-slate-100`) and legend panel backgrounds in `multi-agent-graph.tsx` and `ukb-workflow-graph.tsx`

**Known gap — hardcoded SVG fills:**
- Inline `fill=` / `stroke=` hex attributes on SVG nodes are sourced from `constants.ts` (`NODE_STATUS_COLORS`, `SUBSTEP_COLORS`) as hardcoded hex strings
- Inline attributes are unreachable by CSS class overrides → nodes remain bright in dark mode regardless of theme
- Planned four-phase color-token refactor to close this gap:
  1. Define semantic CSS variable tokens in `index.css`
  2. Create a typed `colors.ts` module for JS/SVG consumption
  3. Extend `tailwind.config.ts` with the new token set
  4. Migrate all constants — eliminating five disconnected color mechanisms (workflow graph, health page, observations, insights, token-usage components)

## Key Files
- `integrations/system-health-dashboard/src/index.css` — global `.dark` CSS override block; authoritative dark-mode source of truth
- `integrations/system-health-dashboard/src/components/workflow/multi-agent-graph.tsx` — `dark:` Tailwind variants for canvas gradient and legend panel
- `integrations/system-health-dashboard/src/components/ukb-workflow-graph.tsx` — same `dark:` treatment as multi-agent-graph
- `integrations/system-health-dashboard/src/constants.ts` — `NODE_STATUS_COLORS`, `SUBSTEP_COLORS` hex constants; primary target of planned color-token migration

## Usage
Dark mode activates when the `.dark` class is present on a parent element (Tailwind class-based dark mode strategy). The CSS override block in `index.css` applies automatically to all covered utility classes within `.dark` scope. Graph components use `dark:` Tailwind variants for their specific canvas and legend overrides.

## Troubleshooting
- **SVG nodes still bright in dark mode**: Known architectural gap — inline `fill=` hex attributes from `constants.ts` cannot be overridden by CSS class rules. Requires the color-token refactor to fix.
- **Status banner unreadable in dark mode**: Locate the relevant status class in the `.dark` block in `index.css`; verify the override selector has sufficient specificity to beat the original rule.
- **Canvas or legend backgrounds not switching**: Check `dark:` Tailwind variants in `multi-agent-graph.tsx` and `ukb-workflow-graph.tsx`; confirm Tailwind's dark mode strategy is set to `class` in `tailwind.config.ts`.
- **White canvas background on Insights or UKB workflow page**: Check `fill-slate-*` and `bg-white` overrides in the `.dark` block of `index.css`.

attributes.name: Dashboard Dark-Mode and Color Token System
attributes.description:
## Purpose
The dashboard UI implements a dark-mode theme through CSS custom properties defined in `src/index.css`. A subset of color references in `constants.ts` use hardcoded hex values that bypass the CSS variable system entirely, causing those elements to fail to adapt when dark mode is active. A central color-token refactor is the planned remediation.

## Architecture
**Theme layer (functional):**
- `src/index.css` defines CSS custom properties for colors, backgrounds, borders, and fills
- Dark-mode retrofit is committed and verified in the compiled CSS bundle
- Components that reference these custom properties adapt automatically on theme toggle

**Hardcoded bypass (open issue):**
- `constants.ts` contains color definitions as raw hex values (e.g., chart fill colors, stroke values)
- These constants are consumed directly by components — no CSS variable resolution occurs at render time
- Components fed by `constants.ts` fills do not respond to dark-mode switching and render with light-mode colors regardless of theme state

**Planned refactor:**
- Migrate all hardcoded hex values in `constants.ts` to reference CSS custom properties/design tokens defined in `src/index.css`
- Until complete, dark-mode rendering is partially correct: theme-aware components adapt; constants-sourced components do not

## Key Files
- `src/index.css` — CSS custom property definitions; primary theme variable source
- `constants.ts` — hardcoded hex fill/color values that bypass the theme (target of pending color-token refactor)

## Usage
- Dark-mode activates the CSS variable set via browser preference or explicit theme toggle
- Correctness of dark-mode rendering is verified by browser inspection: toggle theme and observe whether fill/stroke colors update

## Troubleshooting
- **Elements remain light-colored in dark mode**: Trace the fill/color source for the component — if sourced from `constants.ts`, the color-token refactor is required for that element
- **CSS bundle not reflecting committed theme changes**: The dashboard `dist/` is NOT auto-rebuilt on commit; run `npm run build` explicitly after modifying `src/index.css` or related source files
- **Verify theme variable activation**: In browser DevTools, inspect that CSS custom properties (e.g., `--background`, `--foreground`) reflect dark-mode values when dark mode is active

attributes.name: System Health Dashboard — Theme-Aware Color System
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Provides programmatic, theme-aware color resolution for `system-health-dashboard` components that cannot use CSS variables directly — primarily SVG elements whose `fill=` attributes require concrete hex/rgb values at runtime. A central `lib/colors.ts` module subscribes to theme state and exposes resolved semantic tokens to all programmatic color consumers.

## Architecture
- **SVG limitation**: SVG `fill=` attributes do not resolve CSS variables; any SVG component needing theme-responsive color must obtain resolved values from `lib/colors.ts`, never from CSS variable references.
- **`theme.ts`**: manages current theme state (light/dark) and exposes a subscription pattern consumed by `lib/colors.ts` to react on theme changes.
- **`lib/colors.ts`** (central module, in-progress): subscribes to `theme.ts`; maps semantic status tokens (`success`, `warning`, `error`, `info`, `neutral`) to concrete color values; authoritative source for all programmatic color consumers.
- **Semantic token layer**: tokens defined in both CSS custom properties and Tailwind config; migration sweeps status-meaningful Tailwind classes across Health, Observations, Insights, token-usage, and workflow pages.
- **Dark-mode override block**: interim block retired incrementally — each page must pass a `gsd-browser` visual check before its override is removed.

## Key Files
- `theme.ts` — theme state management and subscription mechanism
- `lib/colors.ts` — central color resolver (in-progress; not yet committed)

## Usage
- SVG components with `fill=` attributes must import resolved values from `lib/colors.ts`.
- All status-bearing pages (Health, Observations, Insights, token-usage, workflow) consume semantic tokens post-migration.
- Verification gate: `gsd-browser` visual check per page before removing that page's dark-mode override block.

## Troubleshooting
- **SVG wrong color after theme switch**: the component is likely referencing a CSS variable in `fill=` rather than subscribing to `lib/colors.ts` updates — CSS variable references in `fill=` silently produce no-ops.
- **Workflow component missing edges**: confirmed isolated to conditional render logic, not color palette values — the color refactor only touched color assignments; debug rendering conditions independently.
- **Dark-mode regressions after override removal**: restore only that page's override block and re-verify in `gsd-browser` before reattempting retirement; do not roll back other pages.

attributes.name: LLM CLI Proxy — Provider Architecture and Restart Behavior
attributes.description:
## Purpose
`proxy-bridge/server.mjs` routes LLM API calls through a tiered provider fallback chain with explicit network-mode-aware routing. Two primary providers are CLI subprocesses with non-trivial cold-start latencies. A direct HTTP/OAuth fast path (`completeClaudeCodeDirect`) exists for `claude-code` and is strongly preferred over CLI invocation when direct Anthropic connectivity is available. Latency signature (~0.9s direct vs ~9.2s CLI) is the primary diagnostic signal for which path was actually used.

## Architecture
**Provider fallback chain (priority order):**
1. **Upstream HTTP proxy** (`proxydetox`, `127.0.0.1:3128`) — preferred path; subject to transient `ECONNREFUSED` when proxydetox goes offline
2. **`claude-code` direct HTTP/OAuth** — `completeClaudeCodeDirect`, `proxy-bridge/server.mjs` lines 441–493; attempted first when external proxy is unavailable but direct Anthropic connectivity exists; ~0.9s latency
3. **Copilot CLI subprocess** (`copilot-provider.ts`) — ~10s cold-start; 15s CLI timeout; preferred when GHE is reachable
4. **Claude Code CLI subprocess** — ~15–20s cold-start; ~9.2s observed when CLI fallback is taken instead of direct OAuth; escalating to this path under a tight caller timeout is dangerous

**Network-mode routing rules:**
- When external connectivity + GHE are both unreachable: `claude-code` is preferred over `copilot`; `completeClaudeCodeDirect` is attempted before any CLI fallback
- `anthropic` provider requires explicit `available: true` in configuration to participate in the chain; defaults to `available: false` — silently absent otherwise
- `processOverride` forces `copilot` provider for the observation-writer process regardless of network mode; this is a separate routing concern, not part of the general fallback chain

**Critical**: both Copilot and Claude Code subprocess paths are shell-spawned CLI processes — not HTTP clients. No outbound TCP connections occur at the provider level.

**Retry logic**: 200ms backoff between provider attempts prevents the self-reinforcing flap loop (transient upstream failure → slow CLI fallback → caller timeout → escalation cascade).

## Key Files
- `proxy-bridge/server.mjs` — main routing logic; `completeClaudeCodeDirect` at lines 441–493; provider fallback chain; retry/backoff logic
- `copilot-provider.ts` — Copilot CLI subprocess provider (~10s cold-start)

## Usage
- All four coding agents (`claude`, `copilot`, `opencode`, `mastra`) route through `rapid-llm-proxy` → `proxy-bridge/server.mjs`
- Network mode is determined upstream by `detectNetworkMode()` (authoritative from health coordinator when reachable; fails open to `"public"`)
- `processOverride` is set per-process externally; observation-writer is permanently pinned to `copilot` by design

## Troubleshooting
- **~9.2s latency instead of ~0.9s**: CLI fallback active instead of `completeClaudeCodeDirect`; check `anthropic` provider `available` flag and verify direct Anthropic OAuth credentials are valid
- **`anthropic` provider inactive**: ensure `available: true` is set explicitly in provider config — the default is `false` and produces no warning
- **Unexpected copilot routing on a process**: check for `processOverride`; observation-writer is always forced to copilot by design
- **ECONNREFUSED on upstream proxy**: proxydetox offline; chain should auto-advance to `completeClaudeCodeDirect` — if not, inspect retry/backoff logic
- **Cold-start timeout cascade**: callers with <15s timeouts will reliably exhaust the Copilot CLI path; set caller timeouts ≥20s to safely accommodate Claude Code CLI as last resort

attributes.name: Multi-Agent Graph — History Mode Edge Rendering
attributes.description:
## Purpose
The multi-agent graph component renders agent workflow topology from two independent sources: nodes from YAML workflow definitions and edges from a hardcoded `MULTI_AGENT_EDGES` constant. These sources use incompatible agent ID strings, causing all edges to be silently dropped in History mode.

## Architecture
- **Node pipeline**: YAML workflow definitions → parser → current agent ID strings → rendered nodes
- **Edge pipeline**: `MULTI_AGENT_EDGES` constant → older/stale agent ID strings → `shouldShowEdge` gate → rendered edges
- **Failure mechanism**: `shouldShowEdge` validates that both source and target node IDs exist in the rendered node set; because `MULTI_AGENT_EDGES` references IDs no longer produced by the YAML parser, every edge fails validation and is discarded silently
- **Scope**: History mode only; the failure is a data mismatch, not a rendering engine defect

## Key Files
- `multi-agent-graph.tsx` — contains `MULTI_AGENT_EDGES` constant and `shouldShowEdge` edge-visibility gate; both are collocated in this file

## Usage
History mode is used to visualize recorded multi-agent execution flows with dataflow wiring between agents. Currently renders nodes at correct positions but with zero connecting edges — the dataflow topology is entirely invisible. No fix has been applied; current state is diagnosis-complete, implementation pending.

## Troubleshooting
- **Symptom**: History mode shows nodes but no connecting edges
- **Root cause**: `MULTI_AGENT_EDGES` agent ID strings are stale; YAML-derived node IDs use newer naming conventions that `MULTI_AGENT_EDGES` does not reflect
- **Diagnosis**: Log or inspect IDs emitted by the YAML workflow parser and compare against string literals in `MULTI_AGENT_EDGES`; any mismatch causes `shouldShowEdge` to discard the edge
- **Fix option A**: Update agent ID strings in `MULTI_AGENT_EDGES` to exactly match current YAML-emitted IDs
- **Fix option B**: Derive edges dynamically from the YAML definitions rather than from the hardcoded constant, eliminating the dual-source divergence entirely

attributes.name: ETM — Observation Artifacts Field Accuracy
attributes.description:
## Purpose
The ETM daemon consumes active session LSL/JSONL transcript files and writes structured observation records used by health monitoring, the System Health Dashboard, and project tracking surfaces. It runs as a persistent background process; agent work continues independently of ETM liveness, meaning ETM failures silently create gaps in the observation record without interrupting the session.

## Architecture
- **Input**: Active session LSL/JSONL transcript files written independently by the Claude runtime; transcripts accumulate even when ETM is down, preserving a full recovery source
- **Output**: Structured observation records committed to the observation store; consumed by the Health Dashboard observations page
- **Liveness signal**: `lastBeat` (assigned at `health-coordinator.js` line 405) reflects the ETM daemon heartbeat — used by the health coordinator to detect daemon status
- **Critical distinction**: `lastBeat` freshness is **not** a user-activity signal; ETM daemon liveness must not be conflated with user presence in the session

## Key Files
- `scripts/enhanced-transcript-monitor.js` — ETM daemon process
- `health-coordinator.js` line 405 — `lastBeat` assignment
- `health-coordinator.js` line ~410 — heartbeat payload containing `transcriptPath` (correct user-activity signal source)

## Usage

attributes.name: ETM Artifact Aggregation and Async Backfill
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Applies two complementary guards between ETM fire paths and the database: turn-scoped semantic dedup prevents observations from distinct user turns from suppressing each other's content, and snapshot promotion upgrades mid-turn progress checkpoints to finals when a matching final arrives. A third guard explicitly exempts `kind:'progress'` observations from dedup entirely, preventing in-progress snapshots from being collapsed into final turn observations.

## Architecture
**Turn-scoped deduplication:**
- `_turnKeyForSet(promptSet)` generates a stable, immutable identifier derived from the prompt-set's first-exchange ID; survives ETM restarts; consistent for the full lifetime of a turn.
- `turnKey` is injected as metadata into both `_firePromptSetObservation` and `_fireBatchObservation` at the ETM fire path.
- `_isSemanticallyDuplicate` restricts duplicate checks to observations sharing the same `turnKey`; cross-turn observations with identical content are not suppressed.

**`kind:'progress'` dedup exemption:**
- Observations tagged `kind:'progress'` are excluded from the 4-hour semantic dedup filter in both directions: they are not checked against existing records, and existing records are not checked against them.
- This is a prerequisite for the token-delta progress emitter — without this exemption, progress snapshots would be silently collapsed into final turn observations (or vice versa) by the similarity filter.

**Snapshot promotion:**
- `_promoteProgressSnapshot` detects existing `kind:'progress'` records whose content hash matches an incoming final observation.
- Upgrades the progress record to a final in-place rather than inserting a duplicate; no hard deletes, preserving store integrity.

## Key Files
- `src/live-logging/ObservationWriter.js` — contains `_isSemanticallyDuplicate`, `_turnKeyForSet`, `_promoteProgressSnapshot`, and the `kind:'progress'` exemption logic

## Usage
Called transparently by all ETM fire paths. `turnKey` and `kind` metadata must be present in the observation payload for correct behavior; callers are responsible for injecting them before the write call.

## Troubleshooting
- **Cross-turn observations being suppressed**: verify `turnKey` is injected at the ETM fire path; a missing or null `turnKey` causes all observations to share a null dedup scope.
- **Progress snapshot collapsed into final**: confirm `kind:'progress'` is set on the observation record before the write; a missing tag subjects the snapshot to normal dedup.
- **Duplicate final + progress records in DB**: `_promoteProgressSnapshot` fires on content-hash match; if hashes differ between progress and final records, promotion will not trigger and both records persist — check content normalization upstream.
- **Same-turn duplicate finals**: same-turn dedup (retries, redundant fires within one turn) is preserved; if duplicates appear within a single turn, check that `turnKey` is stable (not regenerating per-fire).

attributes.name: ObservationWriter — Turn-Scoped Deduplication and Snapshot Promotion
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Prevents cross-turn false-positive semantic deduplication in `ObservationWriter` by scoping duplicate-content checks to a single turn via a stable turn key. Also handles orphaned mid-turn progress snapshots — promoting them to final summaries via content-hash matching — without hard deletes, preserving store integrity.

## Architecture
**Turn-scoped deduplication:**
- `_turnKeyForSet(promptSet)` generates a stable, immutable identifier derived from the prompt-set's first-exchange ID; this survives ETM restarts and is consistent for the full lifetime of a turn
- `turnKey` is injected as metadata into both `_firePromptSetObservation` and `_fireBatchObservation`
- `_isSemanticallyDuplicate` uses `turnKey` to restrict duplicate checks to observations within the same turn; without this scope, semantically similar observations from distinct turns (e.g., repeated housekeeping turns) are incorrectly suppressed as duplicates

**Progress snapshot promotion:**
- `_promoteProgressSnapshot(snapshot)` upgrades orphaned mid-turn progress snapshots to final summaries; an orphan is a progress record with no corresponding final observation
- Matching is done via content-hash comparison between the orphaned snapshot and the candidate final observation
- Promotion uses the store's `validUntil`/`putEntity` supersede pattern (replace-in-place), never hard deletes, preserving store audit semantics

## Key Files
- `src/live-logging/ObservationWriter.js` — `_turnKeyForSet`, `_isSemanticallyDuplicate`, `_promoteProgressSnapshot`, `_firePromptSetObservation`, `_fireBatchObservation`
- `scripts/enhanced-transcript-monitor.js` — ETM integration layer; supplies prompt-set context when calling `_fireBatchObservation` and `_firePromptSetObservation`
- `tests/integration/observation-writer.turn-dedup-reconcile.test.js` — integration test suite (15 Jest tests covering dedup + reconcile paths; 6 ETM artifact aggregation tests)

## Usage
Turn-key injection and semantic dedup fire automatically on every `_firePromptSetObservation` / `_fireBatchObservation` call — no caller configuration required. `_promoteProgressSnapshot` is invoked for any progress record detected as orphaned at turn-completion time. Both mechanisms are transparent to ETM callers.

## Troubleshooting
- **Observations from different turns being suppressed**: Verify `_turnKeyForSet` returns a non-null value; a null `turnKey` collapses dedup to global scope, treating all turns as a single scope and causing cross-turn false positives; root cause is a missing or null first-exchange ID on the prompt-set passed to `_turnKeyForSet`
- **Orphaned progress snapshots persisting in the store**: `_promoteProgressSnapshot` requires a content-hash match between the orphan and the final observation; a mismatch leaves the snapshot unpromoted; inspect hash values on both records to diagnose divergence
- **Unexpected store duplication after promotion**: `_promoteProgressSnapshot` never hard-deletes; if both the original snapshot and the promoted record appear simultaneously, check that `validUntil` was set correctly on the superseded record via `putEntity`
- **Regression check**: run `jest tests/integration/observation-writer.turn-dedup-reconcile.test.js` — all 15 tests must pass; any failure indicates a broken dedup scope or a broken supersede path

attributes.name: ObservationWriter — Semantic Dedup and Snapshot Promotion
attributes.description:
## Purpose
`ObservationWriter.js` applies two complementary guards between ETM and the database. Turn-aware semantic dedup prevents observations from different user turns from suppressing each other's content. Snapshot promotion ensures progress-checkpoint records are upgraded to finals rather than left orphaned when a matching final arrives.

## Architecture
**Turn-aware semantic dedup:**
- `_isSemanticallyDuplicate` is scoped by a stable `turnKey` — the first-exchange UUID of each prompt-set — plumbed from ETM's fire paths into observation metadata before the write call
- Dedup candidates are restricted to observations sharing the same `turnKey`; cross-turn observations with identical content are no longer suppressed
- Same-turn dedup (retries, redundant fires within one turn) is preserved unchanged

**Snapshot promotion:**
- `_promoteProgressSnapshot` detects in-place progress snapshots whose content hash matches an incoming final observation
- Upgrades the progress record to a final in-place via `putEntity` replay semantics (same code path used in artifact patching)
- Prevents progress snapshots from persisting permanently as orphans when the turn completes with matching content

**Conservative design:** Both fixes reduce the dedup candidate set or promote rather than delete, minimizing regression surface.

## Key Files
- `src/live-logging/ObservationWriter.js` — `_isSemanticallyDuplicate` (turn-scoped) and `_promoteProgressSnapshot` helper
- `scripts/enhanced-transcript-monitor.js` — sets `turnKey` (first-exchange UUID of prompt-set) in observation metadata before each fire call
- `tests/integration/observation-writer.turn-dedup-reconcile.test.js` — 4-test integration suite covering turn-dedup scoping and snapshot-promotion behaviors

## Usage
`ObservationWriter` is invoked by ETM on every observation fire — both mid-turn progress fires and final completion fires. The `turnKey` must be set by ETM before the write call; a missing or incorrect `turnKey` re-enables cross-turn suppression. Snapshot promotion runs automatically on final writes with no additional caller configuration.

## Troubleshooting
- **Cross-turn suppression recurring**: verify ETM is setting `turnKey` to the first-exchange UUID of the prompt-set (not the current exchange UUID); inspect the observation fire paths in `enhanced-transcript-monitor.js`
- **Progress snapshots remain orphaned**: promotion requires a content-hash match between the progress and final record — if async LLM enrichment altered the final's content post-progress-fire, hashes will diverge and promotion will not trigger; inspect both records' hashes directly in the DB
- **Run integration tests**: `tests/integration/observation-writer.turn-dedup-reconcile.test.js` — 4 tests cover both failure modes end-to-end

attributes.name: Claude Binary Runtime Dependency
attributes.description:
## Purpose
`coding/bin/coding` is the primary agent runner entry point for the `coding` project. It resolves the `claude` CLI binary via `PATH`, which is supplied by the `claude-code` Homebrew cask. Incomplete cask upgrades can leave a dangling symlink that silently breaks `coding/bin/coding` with no clear error message pointing at the root cause.

## Architecture
- **Resolution chain**: `coding/bin/coding` → `claude` lookup via `PATH` → `/opt/homebrew/bin/claude` (symlink managed by Homebrew) → `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/claude-code/<version>/claude` (actual binary)
- **Failure mode — incomplete cask extraction**: A Homebrew cask upgrade updates the `/opt/homebrew/bin/claude` symlink to point at the new version directory but may fail to extract the binary into `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/claude-code/<version>/`, leaving a dangling symlink; `coding/bin/coding` then fails to start because the resolved path does not exist
- **Manual symlink fix is insufficient**: The binary file itself is absent, not merely misdirected; correcting the symlink target without a reinstall still yields a missing file

## Key Files
- `coding/bin/coding` — agent runner entry point; requires `claude` on `PATH`
- `/opt/homebrew/bin/claude` — Homebrew-managed symlink; inspect with `ls -la /opt/homebrew/bin/claude`
- `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/claude-code/<version>/` — cask extraction directory; must contain the actual `claude` binary after a successful install

## Usage
`coding/bin/coding` is invoked directly to start any agent session. It must be able to exec `claude` before any session logic runs. The dependency is implicit (via `PATH`) rather than an explicit configured path.

## Troubleshooting
- **`coding/bin/coding` fails to start after a `claude-code` upgrade**: Run `ls -la $(which claude)` to check for a dangling symlink, then `ls /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/claude-code/` to confirm the binary is missing from the new version directory
- **Fix — dangling symlink after incomplete cask extraction**: `brew reinstall --cask claude-code`; this re-extracts the full cask and restores the binary
- **Fix — partial Homebrew state**: `brew cleanup claude-code && brew reinstall --cask claude-code` ensures stale artifacts are removed before reinstall
- **Verify resolution**: After reinstall, `claude --version` must succeed and `coding/bin/coding` should start normally in default mode
- **Distinguishing from PATH config issues**: If `which claude` resolves but `claude --version` fails with a "no such file" error, the cause is a dangling symlink, not a PATH misconfiguration

attributes.name: Phase 67 — Reproducibility & Replay Rig
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Builds the foundational `lib/repro/` modules for the GSD reproducibility rig: deterministic LLM fixture recording/replay, environment and git-state capture, KB snapshot assembly, and LLM proxy record/replay taps. These modules underpin the full REPRO-01/REPRO-02 system completed downstream in Phase 75.

## Architecture
Seven plans (67-01 through 67-07) across 3 waves. **4 of 7 plans complete** (Waves 1–2 merged to `main`); Wave 3 plans (67-02, 67-05, 67-07) remain.

**Wave 1 — Fixture primitives and environment capture (Plans 67-01, 67-03):**
- `lib/repro/fixtures/match-key.mjs` — single deterministic match-key design for fixture lookup
- `lib/repro/fixtures/llm-record.mjs` — records LLM request/response pairs as JSONL fixtures
- `lib/repro/fixtures/llm-replay.mjs` — replays fixtures; honest hard-fail on cache miss (no silent fallback)
- `lib/repro/git-state.mjs` — injection-safe, fixed-argv git state capture (sha, dirty patch, untracked files, submodules)
- `lib/repro/env-allowlist.mjs` — allowlist-only env capture with secret-deny regex
- `lib/repro/mcp-inventory.mjs` — live MCP server probe with config fallback
- Redacted transcript fixture produced for Wave 3 downstream use (Plan 67-02)

**Wave 2 — Snapshot assembly and proxy taps (Plans 67-04, 67-06):**
- `captureKb(...)` — byte-exact LevelDB export + atomic JSON write; no live-store mutation
- `captureSnapshot(task_id)` — 9-component manifest with `clock_base`, per-channel maps, `kb_caveat`; `sanitizeTaskId` guards against path traversal (substitutes for missing dist-import)
- Four threat mitigations verified in tests: path traversal, single-owner enforcement, secret leakage, repudiation
- Replay tap: returns recorded response on cache hit; returns HTTP `409` before provider resolution on miss
- Record tap: captures request/response pair on LLM completion
- Documented deviations: NUL byte stripping (before fixture write), D-07 ordinal reset
- Proxy tap implemented in `_work/rapid-llm-proxy/proxy-bridge/server.mjs` (external repo); `coding` worktree for Plan 67-06 holds only `SUMMARY` and self-check documentation

**Security model:** secrets blocked at env-allowlist layer; path traversal blocked by `sanitizeTaskId`; destructive KB restore scoped to isolated worktrees only.

## Key Files
- `lib/repro/fixtures/match-key.mjs` — deterministic match-key generation
- `lib/repro/fixtures/llm-record.mjs` — LLM fixture writer
- `lib/repro/fixtures/llm-replay.mjs` — LLM fixture replayer (hard-fail semantics)
- `lib/repro/git-state.mjs` — injection-safe git state capture
- `lib/repro/env-allowlist.mjs` — allowlist-only environment snapshot
- `lib/repro/mcp-inventory.mjs` — MCP server inventory probe
- `_work/rapid-llm-proxy/proxy-bridge/server.mjs` — proxy record/replay tap (external repo; `coding` worktree holds docs only)
- `.data/run-snapshots/` — snapshot output directory (gitignored)

## Usage
- Call `captureSnapshot(task_id)` to produce a full 9-component reproducibility manifest for any GSD task
- LLM proxy taps activate at `POST /api/complete` in the rapid-llm-proxy runtime; replay mode returns fixture or `409` before provider resolution
- `lib/repro/fixtures/` modules consumed by Wave 3 plans (67-02, 67-05, 67-07) and the downstream regression harness
- Proxy tap changes must be pushed separately to `_work/rapid-llm-proxy` (HTTPS-only remote); see Multi-Repo Git Coordination insight

## Troubleshooting
- Replay tap returns HTTP `409` (not a silent passthrough) on fixture cache miss — ensure a record pass ran first and fixture files are present in the expected location
- NUL bytes are stripped from LLM responses before fixture write; if fixture content appears truncated, this is the documented NUL-stripping deviation, not corruption
- `sanitizeTaskId` rejects `..`, `/`, and special characters in task IDs — normalize IDs before calling `captureSnapshot`
- Wave 3 (plans 67-02, 67-05, 67-07) depends on Wave 1–2 merge; confirm no open worktrees from prior waves before dispatching Wave 3

Seven plans (67-01 through 67-07) across 3 waves. **4 of 7 plans complete** (Waves 1–2 merged to `main`); Wave 3 plans (67-02, 67-05, 67-07) remain.

**Wave 1 — Fixture primitives and environment capture (Plans 67-01, 67-03):**
- `lib/repro/fixtures/match-key.mjs` — single deterministic match-key design for fixture lookup
- `lib/repro/fixtures/llm-record.mjs` — records LLM request/response pairs as JSONL fixtures
- `lib/repro/fixtures/llm-replay.mjs` — replays fixtures; honest hard-fail on cache miss (no silent fallback)
- `lib/repro/git-state.mjs` — injection-safe, fixed-argv git state capture (sha, dirty patch, untracked files, submodules)
- `lib/repro/env-allowlist.mjs` — allowlist-only env capture with secret-deny regex
- `lib/repro/mcp-inventory.mjs` — live MCP server probe with config fallback
- Redacted transcript fixture produced for Wave 3 downstream use (Plan 67-02)

**Wave 2 — Snapshot assembly and proxy taps (Plans 67-04, 67-06):**
- `captureKb(...)` — byte-exact LevelDB export + atomic JSON write; no live-store mutation
- `captureSnapshot(task_id)` — 9-component manifest with `clock_base`, per-channel maps, `kb_caveat`; `sanitizeTaskId` guards against path traversal (substitutes for missing dist-import)
- Four threat mitigations verified in tests: path traversal, single-owner enforcement, secret leakage, repudiation
- Replay tap: returns recorded response on cache hit; returns HTTP `409` before provider resolution on miss
- Record tap: captures request/response pair on LLM completion
- Documented deviations: NUL byte stripping (before fixture write), D-07 ordinal reset
- Proxy tap implemented in `_work/rapid-llm-proxy/proxy-bridge/server.mjs` (external repo); `coding` worktree for Plan 67-06 holds only `SUMMARY` and self-check documentation

**Security model:** secrets blocked at env-allowlist layer; path traversal blocked by `sanitizeTaskId`; destructive KB restore scoped to isolated worktrees only.

## Key Files
- `lib/repro/fixtures/match-key.mjs` — deterministic match-key generation
- `lib/repro/fixtures/llm-record.mjs` — LLM fixture writer
- `lib/repro/fixtures/llm-replay.mjs` — LLM fixture replayer (hard-fail semantics)
- `lib/repro/git-state.mjs` — injection-safe git state capture
- `lib/repro/env-allowlist.mjs` — allowlist-only environment snapshot
- `lib/repro/mcp-inventory.mjs` — MCP server inventory probe
- `_work/rapid-llm-proxy/proxy-bridge/server.mjs` — proxy record/replay tap (external repo; `coding` worktree holds docs only)
- `.data/run-snapshots/` — snapshot output directory (gitignored)

## Usage
- Call `captureSnapshot(task_id)` to produce a full 9-component reproducibility manifest for any GSD task
- LLM proxy taps activate at `POST /api/complete` in the rapid-llm-proxy runtime; replay mode returns fixture or `409` before provider resolution
- `lib/repro/fixtures/` modules consumed by Wave 3 plans (67-02, 67-05, 67-07) and the downstream regression harness
- Proxy tap changes must be pushed separately to `_work/rapid-llm-proxy` (HTTPS-only remote); see Multi-Repo Git Coordination insight

## Troubleshooting
- Replay tap returns HTTP `409` (not a silent passthrough) on fixture cache miss — ensure a record pass ran first and fixture files are present in the expected location
- NUL bytes are stripped from LLM responses before fixture write; if fixture content appears truncated, this is the documented NUL-stripping deviation, not corruption
- `sanitizeTaskId` rejects `..`, `/`, and special characters in task IDs — normalize IDs before calling `captureSnapshot`
- Wave 3 (plans 67-02, 67-05, 67-07) depends on Wave 1–2 merge; confirm no open worktrees from prior waves before dispatching Wave 3

attributes.name: Run Model Attribution — Span Pipeline and Foreground Agent Tracking
attributes.description:
## Purpose
`scripts/measurement-stop.mjs` orchestrates all finalization work that executes when a GSD measurement span closes (`/gsd close`). Runs observation-ref enrichment, per-turn context file compression, raw-body file compression, and token/observation correlation in a strictly defined sequence. It is the primary extension point for span-close lifecycle work in the performance measurement pipeline.

## Architecture
Four responsibilities executed at span-close in strict sequential order:
1. **`enrichObservationRefs`** — joins `context-turns.jsonl` records with run observations via a time-window + agent correlation strategy, populating `observation_ref` fields initialized as `null` at proxy request time. Deferral to span-close is intentional: enrichment at request time risks finding no observations yet, producing permanently null refs.
2. **`closeContextTurns` gzip** — compresses `context-turns.jsonl` → `context-turns.jsonl.gz`; deletes the plaintext original to reduce storage footprint.
3. **Raw-body file compression** — compresses raw request/response body files accumulated during the span.
4. **Token/observation correlation** — correlates token usage records with observation data across the full span.

## Key Files
- `scripts/measurement-stop.mjs` — span-close lifecycle orchestrator; primary extension point for new span-close work
- `context-turns.jsonl` / `context-turns.jsonl.gz` — per-turn context records; plaintext compressed and deleted at step 2
- Observation data files — enriched with `observation_ref` fields during step 1

## Usage
Triggered automatically by `/gsd close`. Not invoked directly by operators or sub-agents. All four steps run sequentially; downstream analytics and reporting depend on the correlation and compression outputs being present before querying span data.

## Troubleshooting
- **`observation_ref` fields remain `null` after close**: Time-window missed observations. Check tolerance in `enrichObservationRefs` and verify observation files are present at close time.
- **`context-turns.jsonl.gz` missing**: Compression step failed — confirm `context-turns.jsonl` existed, was readable, and sufficient disk space was available.
- **Correlation step produces empty output**: Token records or observation data absent. Verify both upstream sources completed before `/gsd close` was issued.
- **Adding new span-close lifecycle work**: Extend `measurement-stop.mjs` with a new step after the existing four, or before step 4 if the new data must feed into correlation.

attributes.name: Foreground Task Token Capture — Route Architecture
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Documents confirmed caching behavior per agent backend and the resulting measurement asymmetry in the performance dashboard. Cache metadata availability varies structurally by backend — not all zero-cache observations are capture gaps. Defines reconciliation requirements across the proxy capture layer, token-adapter ingestion, and dashboard query layer before cross-agent cache comparisons are valid.

## Architecture
**`cache_read` token semantic:**
- `cache_read` tokens are re-transmitted over the wire on every API call — the full cached prefix is always included in the request body.
- Provider billing is ~0.1× because Anthropic caches the *computation* (KV prefix cache keyed on prefix content hash), not the byte transmission.
- This is a provider-side computation cache, not a data-transmission optimization.

**Per-agent measurement status:**

| Agent | Cache Capture | Route | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude | Full (reads + writes per turn) | Wire-tap at `/v1/messages` | Confirmed |
| Other agents | Status varies | — | Full per-agent table partially confirmed; consult active investigation for non-Claude agents |

- **Three-layer reconciliation requirement**: Proxy capture layer → token-adapter ingestion → dashboard query layer must all be aligned before cross-agent cache comparisons are trustworthy.

## Key Files
- Proxy capture layer (path not confirmed) — wire-taps `/v1/messages` for Claude agent token metadata.
- Token adapter (path not confirmed) — ingests captured metadata into the dashboard data store.
- Dashboard query layer — surfaces per-agent cache data; asymmetry is visible here first.

## Usage
Consulted when diagnosing zero-cache observations in the performance dashboard. Determines whether a zero value reflects a genuine cache miss, a capture gap, or a structural measurement limitation for a given backend. Required reading before drawing cross-agent cache performance conclusions.

## Troubleshooting
- **Zero cache values for Claude agent**: Likely a genuine cache miss or proxy capture gap — check wire-tap at `/v1/messages` is active and capturing metadata for the session in question.
- **Zero cache values for non-Claude agents**: May be structural (backend does not expose cache metadata) rather than a capture gap — confirm per-agent measurement status before investigating further.
- **Cross-agent cache comparisons appear inconsistent**: Reconcile all three layers (proxy, adapter, query) before drawing conclusions; asymmetry is by design for backends that do not expose cache metadata.

attributes.name: Agent Proxy Routing — Launcher Integration
attributes.description:
## Purpose
A performance-dashboard modal that exposes per-turn context-window anatomy, service topology, and cache token asymmetry across agent backends. Designed to surface the structural difference between Claude (full cache metadata: reads + writes per turn) and OpenCode (zero cache metrics by design).

## Architecture
**Redux integration:**
- `explainTaskId` reducer/selector in `performanceSlice.ts`; trigger button in `runs-table.tsx`; `Dialog` mounted in `performance.tsx`
- Mirrors the `overrideTaskId` / score-drawer pattern for consistent modal lifecycle management

**Four display regions:**
1. **Service topology strip** — visualizes agent → LLM proxy → Docker + backend chain; ETM, obs-cli, and constraint bundle are *parallel independent clients* of the LLM proxy, not downstream consumers of chat-proxy output — this distinction must be preserved in rendering
2. **Context-window anatomy band** — horizontal segmented bar; byte-level segment sizes sourced from proxy-bridge per-turn data
3. **Cache token asymmetry panel** — displays cache read/write deltas per turn; Claude provides full metadata, OpenCode provides zero cache metrics by design
4. *(fourth region not fully documented)*

## Key Files
- `performanceSlice.ts` — `explainTaskId` reducer and selector
- `runs-table.tsx` — trigger button that dispatches modal open
- `performance.tsx` — `Dialog` mount point for the modal

## Usage
- Accessed from the performance dashboard via the trigger button in the runs table
- Consumed by developers and operators analyzing per-turn cache efficiency and context-window composition across agent runs
- ETM, obs-cli, and constraint bundle must always be rendered as parallel LLM proxy clients — not as consumers downstream of chat-proxy

## Troubleshooting
- **Modal does not open**: Inspect `explainTaskId` in Redux DevTools; verify trigger button in `runs-table.tsx` dispatches the correct action
- **Service topology misrendered** (ETM/obs-cli shown as downstream of chat-proxy): Correct the topology rendering — these are parallel independent LLM proxy clients, not chat-proxy consumers
- **OpenCode cache fields show zero**: Expected and correct by design — OpenCode does not emit cache metadata; zero values are not a data pipeline error

attributes.name: ETM Exchange Parser — Message Type Recognition
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Classifies every record in a Claude session transcript JSON as a user prompt, assistant response, or non-prompt entry. Unrecognized record types are silently dropped — no error raised, no placeholder inserted — producing invisible gap windows in the observation record and skewing downstream metrics.

## Architecture
Three structurally distinct user-prompt variants exist in transcript JSON:

1. **`type: user`** — Standard prompt; content nested inside the message structure. Primary supported type. Fully handled by both parsers.
2. **`type: queue-operation` + `operation: enqueue`** — Interrupt prompt sent while the assistant is mid-turn; content lives at the **top level** of the record, not nested. Mutually exclusive with `type: user` per prompt — no cross-type deduplication needed. Fully supported in both parsers (`extractExchanges` in ETM and the backfill script).
3. **Image-attached messages** — Prompts containing image attachments are silently skipped by both parsers. An open known gap: affected turns produce no observation and the gap is invisible in the observation record.

Parser changes must always be propagated to both files in parallel. The lower-risk validation path is to implement and verify in `backfill-gap-observations.mjs` first, then port to `enhanced-transcript-monitor.js`.

## Key Files
- `scripts/enhanced-transcript-monitor.js` — live ETM daemon; `extractExchanges()` function owns message type classification; primary production parser
- `scripts/backfill-gap-observations.mjs` — offline replay script; identical message type logic; used to validate parser changes at lower risk and to recover observations missed during ETM downtime or parser gaps
- `memory/reference_queue_operation_prompts.md` — reference documentation for the `queue-operation` edge case and its structural differences from `type: user`; consult before modifying parser logic

## Usage
- ETM runs continuously as a launchd-managed daemon, parsing the active session transcript in near-real-time and emitting observations to obs-api (`:12436`)
- The backfill script is run manually after gap windows are detected; it replays transcript ranges to recover missed observations
- Any new message type identified in raw transcripts requires a coordinated update to both files before observations will be captured for that type

## Troubleshooting
- **Invisible observation gap**: inspect raw transcript JSON for records that don't match `type: user` or (`type: queue-operation` + `operation: enqueue`). Image-attached prompts are the most common current culprit.
- **`queue-operation` prompts missing**: verify `extractExchanges` in both files reads content from the record's **top level**, not from a nested message field — the structural difference from `type: user` is the source of the historical blind spot.
- **Image-attached message gaps**: no parser support currently exists; affected observations must be noted manually or backfilled once parser support is added. Cross-reference `memory/reference_queue_operation_prompts.md` for structural patterns.
- **Spurious duplicates after a parser fix**: `queue-operation` vs `type: user` deduplication is not needed (types are mutually exclusive per prompt); if duplicates appear, the issue is in `ObservationWriter.js` turn-aware dedup, not the parser.
