## 7. Risks and unknowns

**R1 — Read-only mount vs tools that write beside the repo. Highest risk; blocks everything.** All three candidates default to a repo-local index (`.codegraph/`, `.code-review-graph/graph.db`; only `codebase-memory` documents `CBM_CACHE_DIR`). Escalation ladder: (a) documented env/flag; (b) different cwd + explicit target arg; (c) nested writable mount over the ro path — `- ${CODING_REPO:-.}/.data/<tool>/repo-local:/workspace/coding/.<tool>` works (a nested bind over a `:ro` parent is writable) but pollutes the workspace namespace and only covers `/workspace/coding`; (d) copy the repo into a writable dir — costs disk and breaks git-based freshness. **Spike per backend before any Dockerfile work.** Note this also caps any future ambition to benchmark other repos under `/workspace` (`${HOME}/Agentic:/workspace:ro`).

**R2 — stdio transport, and a repo-specific SQLite hazard.** stdio via `docker exec -i` means: a container exec per agent session (M5 in the gate); hard failure instead of graceful degradation when the container is down; a docker-socket dependency wherever the agent runs; and **concurrent agent sessions each opening the same SQLite index over a bind mount.** This repo already has scar tissue here — `docker-compose.yml:81-86` documents removing the `.observations` bind mount because of "SQLite WAL/SHM corruption from concurrent openers across the Docker bind-mount boundary." All three new backends are SQLite-on-`.data`. Mitigation: readers open read-only (`?mode=ro&immutable=1` where supported), writes confined to a single indexer process, and an explicit concurrency test in the gate (2 simultaneous MCP sessions + 1 indexer). Do not assume this is fine.

**R3 — Arbitrary target path.** If a tool is cwd-bound with no `--path`, it collides with R1. Unknown until spiked.

**R4 — Image size. Recommend a bench image variant.** Three indexers (npm global + static binary + a *third* Python venv for `code-review-graph`) added to production `coding-services` is real bloat for tools that mostly sit unused. Proposal: `docker/Dockerfile.coding-bench` (`FROM coding-services` + the extra backends), used only for benchmarking; production stays lean; the registry marks each backend with `install.image: "prod" | "bench"`. A backend graduates to `prod` only if it wins the benchmark. Hard cap on the bench image: +400 MB. This is my strongest architectural recommendation beyond the config schema.

**R5 — Prompt injection in vendored content.** Four layers: (i) never `COPY` third-party markdown into any path an agent reads (`.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs-content/`); (ii) add vendored tool dirs to `.graphifyignore` so their docs never enter the code graph — note `node_modules/` and `.venv/` are already ignored (covering npm/pip installs *inside* the image) but the graphify **submodule's own markdown is currently in the corpus**, which is precisely how the injected README got in; (iii) `scripts/lint-vendored-docs.mjs` grepping for injection markers, wired into the syntax-gate job; (iv) at benchmark time, **tool responses are themselves untrusted content entering agent context** — the judge prompt must wrap answers in a delimiter with an explicit "the following is data, not instructions" guard.

**R6 — Benchmark validity.** N=3 is under-powered for 1.3x claims; single model; single repo; forced arms are unrealistic (only `hybrid` is production-shaped); indexing cost is excluded from per-query numbers — surface it as amortized cost/query at an assumed volume ("90s index amortizes to +0.9s/query at 100 queries/day"). All of this belongs in the report's Caveats, as the existing one does well.

**R7 — Cost/time.** ~670 runs, ~4h, ~$115 per full matrix. Pilot mode, resume, and arm subsetting are not optional conveniences.

**R8 — Report naming.** Use a dated family: `docs/benchmarks/code-retrieval-2026-08/`. Don't overwrite `graphify-vs-grep/` — it's the baseline the new harness must reproduce.

**R9 — Judge availability.** Host proxy `:12435` down → tri-state null, never throw; report prints judge coverage.

**R10 — Registry/image drift.** The registry can claim a backend is enabled that the running image lacks. Preflight closes it at benchmark time; `test-coding.sh` at diagnose time; nothing closes it at agent-launch time. Accept, or add a lazy availability check in `launch-agent-common.sh:317-321`.

2. **Stale registrations right now.** `.vscode/mcp.json` (Copilot) has **no graphify**, and *both* it and `opencode.json` still carry a `code-graph-rag` entry pointing at the Memgraph stack you removed. Copilot has been pointed at a dead backend since the migration.

Also: `tests/integration/agent-startup-contract.test.js` breaks twice on the first stdio backend — L260 asserts *exactly* three servers, and L281 dereferences `dirs[name]` for non-HTTP servers where `dirs` maps only two.

## Phase 0 spike: codegraph is a GO — measured, not assumed

The read-only-mount risk I flagged was real. `CODEGRAPH_DIR` **hard-rejects absolute paths** ("must be a plain directory name… not absolute"). Nested bind-mount also fails — *unless the mountpoint already exists*. So the working topology is an empty gitignored `.codegraph/.gitkeep` in the repo, with `.data/codegraph` bound over it. Verified on the real repo: the DB landed in `.data/codegraph/`, the repo mount stayed untouched.

| | codegraph | graphify (context) |
|---|--:|--:|
| Cold index | **22.0s** parse / 36s wall | minutes |
| Incremental sync | **1s** | ~14s post-fix |
| Nodes / edges | 27,020 / **85,894** | 57,416 / 80,913 |
| Artifact | 111 MB SQLite (WAL) | ~62 MB JSON |

It comfortably clears every drop threshold. Three things worth knowing:

- **The corpus scopes differ** — codegraph indexed 1,599 files (code only) vs graphify's code+docs+PDFs. Node counts aren't comparable at face value; that's a fairness caveat for the report, not a win for either.
- **`codegraph serve --mcp` is a hidden command** — absent from `--help`, works fine. The article was right and the tool's own help is wrong.
- **`codegraph init` ends with an interactive prompt**, which would hang under supervisord. Needs `</dev/null`; freshness gets driven by the reindex dispatcher, not its git hooks.

## Working tree

I created `.codegraph/.gitkeep` and added three `.gitignore` entries — the mountpoint the topology requires. Nothing else is modified; no commit yet.

Next up is Phase 1: the backend registry plus the two prerequisite fixes above. Worth flagging that the install.sh converter fix and the stale `code-graph-rag` purge are independently valuable — they repair Copilot's code-graph wiring whether or not the rest of this lands, so I'd commit them as their own change.

## How this was reconstructed

| KB insight (the methodology) | `insights.json` → id `019fd06a-3fab-78ce-b177-18748bd1e9d9`, "Code-Graph/Code-Memory Tool Evaluation — Skeptical Verification Research" |
| KB insight (PDF phase) | `insights.json` → id `019fd02f-d5a7-7708-b25e-c64d1e0b6517`, "Memory System Comparison Research" |
| KB digests | `digests.json` → `d67efc03…` (PDF/web research), `6ecc2790…` (final synthesis), `6aa55ca4…` (viewer + fact-checking), `42534d8c…`/`03efa161…` (kgbench runs) |
| Migration history | digests `bcb150b4…`, `0d44e743…`, `d32aea51…`, `41d638f3…`, `7e5c4252…`, `e0eb8107…`, `6376e1fb…`; insight `019fcb80…` "Code-Graph-RAG to Graphify Migration" |

**Important:** the four subagent reports themselves were written to `/private/tmp/claude-502/.../a28150f4-.../tasks/*.output` — **that directory no longer exists**. What survives is the assistant's condensed relay of each verdict in the LSL plus the observation/digest records. No comparison matrix document was ever written to the repo (confirmed: only `docs/benchmarks/graphify-vs-grep/` exists; `.planning/research/` has nothing from August).

---

## 1. What triggered this

Yesterday 2026-08-04 07:23 CEST, the prompt was:

> *"investigate this: `/Users/…/Downloads/Knowledge_memory.pdf` — what options are there for memory systems and how do they compare. Research from the web to see what differences there are (technology, features, etc.). Ideally, I would like to be able to test integrate them all and compare, gain some real insights (performance)."*

`Knowledge_memory.pdf` is **2.1 MB, ~20 pages**, dated Aug 4 07:16 (read as pages 1-10 then 11-20; today's session re-read it as 1-12 + 13-24). Its **text was never dumped into any log** — the PDF is passed to the model as images, so the LSL only records "PDF pages extracted". What *is* recoverable is the article's claim-set, because every claim was quoted verbatim into the four verification prompts. **The PDF is a Medium-style article surveying five code-knowledge-graph/memory tools for AI coding agents**, framed around three variables (technology, features, data-residency/maturity), with these framing claims:

- "~80% of enterprise retrieval queries are simple semantic lookups, 15% need structured multi-hop, 5% need agentic multi-step planning"
- Anthropic's Claude Code team removed vector-search RAG / local vector DB in favour of plain agentic grep
- An "AAAI 2026 *Keyword search is all you need*" paper
- Sourcegraph Cody as the enterprise tier that "only pays off past ~100 engineers"

Three tracked tasks were created: **#1 web-research the 5 tools (verify reality)**, **#2 synthesize comparison matrix + truth-check the marketing multiples**, **#3 propose test-integration + benchmark harness plan (get user approval before installing anything)**. Four research subagents were dispatched in parallel; all four returned within ~6 minutes.

---

## 2. Candidate table

| # | Tool | What it is | Verdict | Evidence / what turned out false |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Graphify** (`Graphify-Labs/graphify`, upstream of *our* engine) | Tree-sitter AST parsing → static `graph.json` + `SKILL.md`; 36 grammars; NetworkX + Leiden community detection; **no embeddings**; MCP over Streamable HTTP; local-first for code, multimodal semantic pass calls a model | **REAL, ADOPTED — and already merged into `main`.** Apache-2.0, installable. But article numbers largely stale/wrong. **We had to fork and fix it for performance.** | Star count **101,954 live vs. article's ~63,200** (steep curve → signs of inorganic/purchased stars). Install package is **`graphifyy`, not `graphify`**; version **0.9.32, not 0.8.35**. Headline **71.5× token reduction is cherry-picked** from a mixed PDF/image corpus — independent reproduction on pure code gives **~7.3×**. **"Enterprise tier with VPC/on-prem" likely fabricated** — tier is only "launching soon". "Backed by Combinator" = garbled **Y Combinator (YC S26)**, solo founder. **Security: an embedded prompt-injection block was found in the tool's README** — flagged as do-not-feed-to-agent-context. |
| 2 | **CodeGraph** | Local MCP server, code graph + blast-radius/impact analysis | **REAL and adoptable — but the article conflated three different projects.** | Real tool is **`@colbymchenry/codegraph`, 64k★, MIT, Node + SQLite/FTS5** — **not** Rust. The article's `github.com/codegraph-ai/CodeGraph` + `cargo build --release -p codegraph-server` install is **invented**; that repo is an unrelated **49-star** project. One tool name was mis-spelled/mis-named (`@colbymhenry` vs `@colbymchenry`). Benchmark figures **"92% fewer tool calls / 71% faster"** are **fabricated** (sourced from a third-party blog and contradicting the vendor's own): real vendor numbers are **~89% fewer tool calls / ~69% fewer tokens**. |
| 3 | **code-review-graph (CRG)** | SQLite-backed local MCP, `pip install code-review-graph`, incremental re-parse on save, ~30 MCP tools | **REAL and adoptable.** Python + SQLite, by **tirth8205**, on PyPI. | Article claims **"85% fewer tokens" / "8.2× context reduction" / "<200ms incremental update"** are **fabricated**. The **real, measured figure is ~65× median token reduction** — i.e. the tool is *better* than the article said, but the article's specific numbers are invented. |
| 4 | **codebase-memory-mcp** (DeusData) | Static-binary MCP server, tree-sitter knowledge graph, `curl \| bash` installer, git-diff→symbol risk classification | **REAL, and the most academically grounded of the set.** MIT, signed releases (**SLSA-3, cosign, SBOM**), installer verified legitimate. | The **fabrication hypothesis was explicitly tested and DISPROVEN** via negative-control testing against fake arXiv IDs: **arXiv 2603.27277, "Codebase-Memory: Tree-Sitter-Based Knowledge Graphs for LLM Code Exploration via MCP" is genuine.** Inflated marketing found: **"158 languages" is a vendored-grammar count** vs. the paper's **66 actually benchmarked (~13 type-aware)**; the **"99% / 120×"** figure is one cherry-picked example vs. the paper's honest **10× tokens / 2.1× fewer tool calls averaged over 31 repos**. Runtime "100% local / no network" and the git-diff risk classification are **plausible but not independently audited**. |
| 5 | **Sourcegraph Cody / Amp** | Enterprise code-intelligence tier | **REAL but repositioned — effectively out of scope for a solo/small-team setup.** | **Cody is now enterprise-only**; consumer Cody Free/Pro was discontinued **Jul 2025**; **Amp** is the individual-tier successor. Air-gapped / self-hosted / SOC2 all **verified real**. The **"~100 engineers" break-even is the author's inference, not a cited figure**. |
| — | **code-graph-rag (CGR) + Memgraph** | *Previous incumbent* — Python submodule + live Memgraph graph DB (bolt 7687, lab UI 3100) | **REMOVED / REPLACED (decision already executed, PR #4 merged).** | Replaced by graphify because it required a Python venv on the host + a live database container. Audit found **40+ reference points across 8 areas**. Risk assessment: removal safe — all consumers (`CodeGraphAgent`, UKB workflows, wave-analysis agents) already degrade gracefully via TCP probes/try-catch, **zero tests depended on live Memgraph**. |
| — | **Plain agentic grep** (the baseline arm) | Glob/Grep/Read only | **The benchmark's surprise winner on reliability and cost.** | See §4. |

---

## 3. What the "skeptical verification" process concluded

The methodology is captured as a reusable insight (`019fd06a-3fab-78ce-b177-18748bd1e9d9`): dispatch one research subagent **per candidate**, each independently verifying **a specific category of claim** (star count, install package name/version, benchmark numbers, license, feature-tier claims, underlying research paper) **against primary sources** — GitHub API, npm/PyPI registries, pypistats, star-history, arXiv API, raw install scripts, YC pages — never the tool's own marketing copy. **Negative-control testing** (querying fake arXiv IDs) is used to separate genuinely fabricated claims from real-but-exaggerated ones.

**Claims that turned out FALSE or fabricated:**

1. Graphify's install command and package name (`graphify` → actually `graphifyy`) and version (0.8.35 → actually 0.9.32).
2. Graphify's "Enterprise tier with VPC/on-prem" — not launched.
3. Graphify's 71.5× token reduction as a general figure — cherry-picked; ~7.3× on pure code.
4. Graphify's star count as stated — plus the live count itself looks inorganic.
5. "Backed by Combinator" — garbled Y Combinator.
6. CodeGraph's Rust/`cargo build` install and `codegraph-ai/CodeGraph` home — invented; three same-named projects conflated.
7. CodeGraph's "92% / 71%" benchmark — fabricated; real ~89% / ~69%.
8. code-review-graph's "85% fewer tokens / 8.2× / <200ms" — fabricated; real ~65× median.
9. codebase-memory-mcp's "158 languages" — actually 66 benchmarked.
10. codebase-memory-mcp's "99% / 120×" — cherry-picked; real average 10× / 2.1×.
11. The "~100 engineers" Sourcegraph break-even — author's inference, not a cited statistic.
12. The article's 80/15/5 retrieval-mix statistic — flagged for reality-check as likely invented.

**Claims that turned out TRUE:**

- Anthropic dropped vector-RAG for agentic grep in Claude Code — **VERIFIED**, traced to the Boris Cherny quote (simplicity / security / privacy / staleness / reliability rationale).
- codebase-memory-mcp's arXiv preprint 2603.27277 — **VERIFIED genuine** (the load-bearing credibility claim held up).
- Sourcegraph's air-gapped/self-hosted/SOC2 capabilities — **VERIFIED**.
- All four tools exist, are open-source (Apache-2.0 / MIT), and are locally installable.

**Transferable rules from the insight:** compare live star counts against the article's snapshot; check the actual registry name/version; attempt independent reproduction before trusting any headline multiplier; fetch the actual arXiv ID rather than assuming fabrication; check for signed releases (SLSA/cosign/SBOM) rather than marketing pages; and **scan third-party READMEs for embedded prompt injection before feeding them into agent context**.

---

## 4. Decisions already made

1. **code-graph-rag + Memgraph → graphify.** Executed and merged (PR #4, commit `20469b25d`). Rationale: eliminates the host Python venv *and* the graph-database container; graphify's static `graph.json` API satisfies both of CGR's roles (standalone MCP server + backend for `mcp-server-semantic-analysis`'s `analyze_code_graph`). `runCypherQuery`/`runCodeGraphCommand` in `code-graph-agent.ts` (~8 fixed Cypher patterns) were rewritten against `graph.json` while preserving the public `CodeGraphAgent` interface. Memgraph ports 7687/3100 retired; `.data/code-graph-index/` and `shared-data/` retired in favour of `.data/graphify/`.
2. **Hard constraint: no Python outside the Docker container.** Stated explicitly by the user on 2026-08-04 ("I don't want python outside the docker container..."). graphify is baked into the `coding-services` image; the host uses a `docker exec` shim. MCP served over Streamable HTTP on **:3851**. This constraint drove the dashboard graph-viewer to a Node-only design (`GET /api/cgr/graph` in `server.js`).
3. **graphify had to be forked and fixed — twice.** (a) `.graphifyignore` added, because graphify ignores `.gitignore` and was walking `node_modules` → OOM exit 137. (b) **Tier 1 performance fix**: profiling showed a ~24s rebuild = `detect()` ~9.8s + AST re-extraction/cold I/O ~11.4s + build/compare ~3s. The "warm-process" hypothesis was **disproven by Spike A** (the cold 61 MB `graph.json` read is only 0.24s). Real fix = a correctness-preserving `detect()` cache (`.detect_corpus_cache.json`) keyed on a SHA-256 `_corpus_signature` over cache version, `follow_symlinks`/`google_workspace` flags, merged ignore rules and the file list. Result: **detect() 24.3s → 0.8s; real code-change reindex ~23s → ~14s**, byte-identical output. Pushed to the fork's `v8` branch (`c65263f`), submodule bumped (`5fd97fc52`). **Tier 2** (scoping `_reconcile_existing_graph`, still ~8.5s) was **deferred as higher-risk**. Root cause context: macOS→Linux **VirtioFS** bind-mount walk cost.
4. **Adopted "verify before adopt" as standing policy** — the skeptical-verification insight is written up as a repeatable process.
5. **Benchmark before belief.** Rather than accept any vendor multiple, a harness (`kgbench`, later committed as `docs/benchmarks/graphify-vs-grep/`) was built: `N queries × M arms × R reps`, deterministic graders for factual queries + LLM-judge for open-ended ones.
6. **Result of that benchmark (this is the big one):**

   | Arm | median tool-calls | median tokens | median latency | mean cost | hard-fail rate | correctness |
   |---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
   | grep | 2 | 218,828 | 19s | $0.157 | **0/27 (0%)** | **1.00** |
   | graph | 2 | 221,970 | 16s | $0.188 | 2/27 (7%) | 0.94 (0.98 completed-only) |

   **The article's 5–70× token multiples did not reproduce.** Rough token parity; graphify **~20% more expensive**; marginally faster median but a **fat latency tail** (a 218s zero-output stall and a hard timeout, both graph-arm — the live MCP dependency adds availability risk stateless grep doesn't have). Reason: **~140k tokens of fixed overhead** (system prompt + tool schemas) dominates every run, compressing total-session ratios; the article measures *content* tokens on huge single queries.
   **But the shape of the win is clear and useful:** graph wins **1.3–2×** on **cross-subsystem lookups (L3, S3)**, **multi-hop blast-radius (B2)**, and the **open-ended architecture question (A1, ~2×, ~2.9× on content tokens alone)**. Grep wins on **single-directory reference listing (S1)** and ties on simple `def` lookups (L1/L2). **Simple-and-local → grep; broad-and-structural → graph.** Caveat: A1's graph answer scored 0.83 vs grep's 1.00 — *compact ≠ complete*.
7. **Report placement convention settled:** `docs/benchmarks/<comparison-name>/README.md`. The report was nearly lost — it lived only in `/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/kgbench/REPORT.md` — and was rescued on 2026-08-05, hardcoded paths stripped, committed via `docs/graphify-vs-grep-benchmark` → merged at `b783ffe2f`.
8. **The graph is now user-visible**: PR #5 added a Code Graph viewer to the system-health dashboard, serving graphify's native `graph.html`, code-only per scope (`1488146d9`). Graph scale reference: **57,416 nodes / 80,913 edges / 4,067 communities** — community-level aggregation is mandatory at that scale; note that **node entity-kind (function/class/method) is not an explicit field** and must be inferred from label shape + edge relations.

---

## 5. Open items / explicit next steps

**From the benchmark README (`docs/benchmarks/graphify-vs-grep/README.md`, "Suggested next steps"):**

1. **Add a hybrid arm** — all tools available, agent chooses. The current arms are *forced* (graph can't fall back to grep), which is not the production mode. This is called out as "the honest production number; cheap to add." ← **highest-value missing measurement**
2. **Harden the graph arm** against the 7% stall — retry-on-timeout in the harness, and investigate the `:3851` MCP stall itself.
3. **Scale the query set** toward harder multi-hop questions and a larger repo, where the graph should separate from grep.
4. **Phase 2: add `codebase-memory-mcp` and `CodeGraph` as extra arms** — explicitly noted as "all verified real, MIT, local." This is the direct continuation of yesterday's work and is *already written down as the plan*.

**Never completed from yesterday:**

5. **Task #2 — the comparison matrix was never written to disk.** The four verification reports were relayed conversationally and their `/private/tmp` output files are gone. Only the KB digest/insight summaries survive. The "Memory System Comparison Research" insight says this explicitly: *"No comparison matrix, candidate shortlist, or integration plan exists yet."*
6. **Task #3 — the test-integration plan was never approved or executed.** Nothing beyond graphify was ever installed. The original instruction was "get user approval before installing anything," and that approval gate was never reached.
7. **Tier 2 graphify optimisation** (`_reconcile_existing_graph`, ~8.5s) deferred.
8. Entity-kind inference layer for `graph.json` consumers — deferred, non-blocking.
9. The article's 80/15/5 retrieval-mix statistic — reality-check was requested but the answer isn't recorded anywhere surviving.

**What today's prompt adds on top** (from `2026-08-05_1700-1800_c197ef.md` line 2114) — the user now wants all candidates integrated into the Docker container + `install.sh` + `scripts/test-coding.sh` + the mac/win/linux CI jobs; one skill per solution; data under `.data/…` as graphify does; a **config to select the active code-graph solution per agent** (claude / opencode / copilot) or use all of them in an `/experiment`; a single combined report in the style of `docs/benchmarks/graphify-vs-grep`; per-query-type routing conclusions (with an explicit warning **not** to bias toward the example "code→grep, docu→graphRAG, architecture→OKF"); each solution tested individually for performance on integration ("the graphify we had to fork and fix"); and a second PDF, **`measure-OKF.pdf`**, as the model for the experiment methodology.</result>

Intent: Understand what `.detect_corpus_cache.json` caches in the graphify engine and what causes cache invalidation
Approach: Examined the detect.py source file to trace the cache file's structure, the `_corpus_signature` function that keys it, and the conditions that trigger cache misses by comparing file lists, ignore rules, flags, and metadata changes
Artifacts: edited imperative-twirling-dragon.md
Result: The cache stores the full corpus manifest (file classifications, counts, ignore/unclassified/sensitive lists, warnings) keyed by a SHA-256 signature. Cache misses occur when the file list changes, ignore rules change, flags flip, the cache version bumps, or (for non-extension-based classification) file mtime/size changes; ordinary code file edits do not invalidate it since classification is path-only.

Read: /Users/<USER_ID_REDACTED>/Agentic/coding/integrations/graphify/graphify/detect.py
Grep: _CORPUS_CACHE_FILE|corpus_cache|_corpus_signature in /Users/<USER_ID_REDACTED>/Agentic/coding/integrations/graphify/graphify/detect.py
Read: /Users/<USER_ID_REDACTED>/Agentic/coding/integrations/graphify/graphify/detect.py

Confirmed against the source. Here's the answer:

`.detect_corpus_cache.json` caches the full output of `detect()`'s per-file classification pass — the corpus manifest (files grouped by `FileType`, total word/file counts, ignored/unclassified/skipped-sensitive lists, warnings) — keyed by a SHA-256 signature (`_corpus_signature`) rather than by content directly, letting a large repo skip the ~9s classification pass on unchanged reindexes (`integrations/graphify/graphify/detect.py:1240-1290,1460-1582`).

A cache miss happens when that signature changes, which is driven by: the sorted file list itself changing (files added/removed/renamed), any `.gitignore`/`.graphifyignore`/`--exclude` rule changing, the `follow_symlinks` or `google_workspace` flags flipping, a bump to `_CORPUS_CACHE_VERSION`, or — for the minority of files whose type isn't determined purely by extension (extensionless shebang files, DOC/OFFICE/<COMPANY_NAME_REDACTED>-Workspace docs) — their mtime or size changing. Editing the *contents* of an ordinary code file (`.py`, `.ts`, etc.) does **not** invalidate it, since code classification is path-only; that file's AST is re-extracted separately by the changed-files rebuild.

This has enough detail to give a precise, sourced answer.

`.detect_corpus_cache.json` caches the *output of `detect()`'s per-file classification pass* (which `FileType` each file in the corpus is — code/doc/image/paper/etc.) — the ~9s classification step, not the cheap file-walk itself (`detect.py:1454-1471`).

attributes.name: kgbench Benchmarking Harness
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Provides complete benchmarking infrastructure for comparing retrieval strategies (grep, graphify, codegraph) across a defined query matrix. Produces structured `results.jsonl` from sequential arm execution with process lifecycle management, failure taxonomy, contamination prevention, stall detection, and a circuit-breaker mechanism.

## Architecture
- **Arms**: 3 active arms (grep, graphify, codegraph) defined in `config/kgbench/arms.json`, loaded by `lib/kgbench/arms.mjs`; topology grounded in `config/code-graph.json`. A **hybrid arm exists in config but is disabled** — enabling it requires verifying `$allBackendTools`/`mcpFrom: [graphify]` config compatibility.
- **Arms adapter layer** (`lib/kgbench/arms.mjs`): builds per-arm agent invocation arguments including `model` and `mcpConfig`; `argvForAgent` is a reusable internal helper.
- **Full matrix**: 16 questions × 3 arms × 3 repeats = 144 cells; each cell = one complete agent session.
- **Matrix sizing**: test arms × questions × replication count determines total cell count before execution begins; must be quantified upfront to set circuit-breaker and timeout budgets.
- **Post-run reporting**: `runner.mjs` and `kgbench-run.mjs` are the primary entry-point and diagnostic scripts; both may be edited during diagnostic passes.

## Key Files
- `kgbench-run.mjs` — top-level benchmark entry point; benchmark integration surface
- `runner.mjs` — run orchestration and diagnostic tooling
- `lib/kgbench/arms.mjs` — arm loading and `argvForAgent` helper
- `config/kgbench/arms.json` — arm definitions (grep, graphify, codegraph, disabled hybrid)
- `config/kgbench/questions/coding-v1.json` — canonical question set; also committed to `docs/benchmarks/graphify-vs-grep/queries.json`

## Usage
Invoked via `kgbench-run.mjs` for full matrix runs. Post-run, a report generation process produces a benchmark report (typically finishing ~5 minutes after the run completes). Log-watcher processes spawned during a run must be manually terminated afterward if not cleaned up automatically — two orphaned watchers are a known post-run artifact.

## Troubleshooting
- **`pkill` watcher exit code 144**: Expected behavior when the log-watcher process is terminated at run end — not a failure signal. These notifications can be safely ignored.
- **Cell count discrepancies**: Always compute `arms × questions × reps` from first principles. The r5 run (228 cells) had a prior off-by-one error reporting 264, caused by double-counting architecture class repetitions on top of a base count that already included their first 3 reps.
- **Orphaned log-watcher processes**: After report generation completes, check for lingering watchers and terminate with `pkill` if present.
- **Tool contamination**: Verify tool isolation post-run by checking that each arm only used its designated tools (e.g., graphify arm: 98/98 cells ok, zero cross-tool contamination).

attributes.name: Graphify Corpus Cache and Ignore Logic
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Graphify caches corpus detection results in `.detect_corpus_cache.json` to avoid repeating an expensive (~9s) file classification pass on every run. Cache validity is keyed by a SHA-256 signature capturing configuration, ignore rules, and file identity.

## Architecture
- **`_corpus_signature`** (`integrations/graphify/graphify/detect.py`): computes SHA-256 over cache format version, `follow_symlinks`/`google_workspace` flags, merged ignore rules, and the full file list.
- **Sole caller**: the `detect` function in the same file — no other call sites exist; any interface change to `_corpus_signature` requires updating only `detect`.
- **Path-deterministic files** (code, paper, image — classified by extension): only the file path is hashed. Body edits do **not** cause a cache miss, enabling fast incremental reindexing.
- **Content-classified files** (extensionless/shebang, DOC, OFFICE, Workspace): path + `mtime_ns` + size is hashed; any content change triggers a cache miss.

- **Cache contents**: `.detect_corpus_cache.json` stores the full corpus manifest — FileType classifications, counts, ignore/unclassified/sensitive lists, and warnings.

## Key Files
- `integrations/graphify/graphify/detect.py` — `_corpus_signature` definition and `detect` function (sole caller)
- `.detect_corpus_cache.json` — runtime cache artifact (repo root or project root); not committed

## Usage
The cache is read and written automatically by `detect()` on every corpus detection pass (cold or warm). The incremental rebuild path in `watch.py` (`_rebuild_code`) calls `detect()` and transparently benefits from cache hits without any special handling.

## Troubleshooting
- **Stale cache after ignore rule change**: delete `.detect_corpus_cache.json` to force a full cold pass (~9s); the signature will mismatch and the cache will be regenerated automatically.

So a miss occurs when: the file set changes (add/remove/rename), any ignore rule changes, the flags change, the cache-version constant is bumped, or a content-classified (non-path-deterministic) file's mtime/size changes.

attributes.name: System Health Dashboard — CGR Reindex API
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Exposes a trigger endpoint for reindexing the code graph from within the system health dashboard backend, allowing dashboard-initiated full reindex operations without direct host-side tooling access.

## Architecture
- **Route**: `POST /api/cgr/reindex` in `integrations/system-health-dashboard/server.js`
- **Mechanism**: Handler spawns `graphify-reindex.sh` to trigger a full corpus re-detection and graph reindex
- This is the **full reindex path** — distinct from the incremental `_rebuild_code` path in `watch.py` which runs automatically on file-watch events
- Sits alongside the 4 existing `/api/cgr/code-*` routes that serve graph data to the Code Graph Viewer iframe
- All routes accessed via reverse-proxy at `:3032`; direct browser calls to `:3033` are a hard architectural violation

## Key Files
- `integrations/system-health-dashboard/server.js` — hosts all `/api/cgr/*` routes including `POST /api/cgr/reindex`; spawns `graphify-reindex.sh`
- `graphify-reindex.sh` — shell script that performs the full reindex; invoked as a child process by the route handler

## Usage
Called by dashboard UI or external tooling via `POST /api/cgr/reindex` (through the `:3032` proxy). Intended for on-demand full reindexes when the incremental watch-loop path is insufficient or the graph is known to be stale.

## Troubleshooting
- **Reindex appears to do nothing**: verify `graphify-reindex.sh` is executable and on the expected path relative to `server.js`; check server logs for spawn errors
- **Route returns 404**: confirm the route is registered in `server.js` and the request is going through `:3032` (proxy), not directly to `:3033`
- **Partial graph after reindex**: the shell script performs a full reindex — if results are partial, check `graphify-reindex.sh` for early-exit conditions or check graphify logs for detection/extraction errors

attributes.name: Intent: Explain what `.detect_corpus_cache.json` caches in the graphify engine a
attributes.description:
Intent: Explain what `.detect_corpus_cache.json` caches in the graphify engine and what causes cache invalidation
Approach: Examined the detect.py implementation to identify cache structure (the `detected` key keyed by fingerprint `sig`), cache hit/miss logic, and the `_corpus_signature` hash inputs—which include format version, flags, ignore rules, and file metadata (paths for deterministic extensions; mtime+size for others)
Artifacts: edited Dockerfile.coding-services
Result: The cache stores corpus classification results (file buckets by type, word counts, ignored/skipped lists). Cache invalidation occurs when the fingerprint changes due to: flag changes (`follow_symlinks`, `google_workspace`), ignore rule modifications, file additions/removals/renames, or content edits to non-path-deterministic files (extensionless/DOC/OFFICE/<COMPANY_NAME_REDACTED>-Workspace files); code file content changes alone do not invalidate since classification is path-only.

Answer in 2-4 sentences.","createdAt":"2026-08-05T18:09:26.932Z","metadata":{"agent":"claude","format":"live"}},{"id":"7406f653-50dc-4bf4-866e-70e541aa296d-assistant","role":"assistant","content":"[Tool calls]
Grep: detect_corpus_cache in .
Grep: detect_corpus_cache|cache_signature|def.*cache|signature in integrations/graphify/graphify/detect.py
Read: /Users/<USER_ID_REDACTED>/Agentic/coding/integrations/graphify/graphify/detect.py
Read: /Users/<USER_ID_REDACTED>/Agentic/coding/integrations/graphify/graphify/detect.py
Grep: cache_file.write|\"sig\"|\"detected\" in integrations/graphify/graphify/detect.py

`.detect_corpus_cache.json` caches the full result of graphify's `detect()` corpus-classification pass (files bucketed by type — CODE/DOCUMENT/PAPER/IMAGE/VIDEO, word counts, ignored/skipped/unclassified lists) under a `detected` key, keyed by a `sig` fingerprint. When the fingerprint matches, `detect()` returns the cached dict directly and skips the ~9s per-file classification pass.

A cache miss (invalidation) happens when the fingerprint (`_corpus_signature`) changes, which is a hash over:
- the cache-format version, `follow_symlinks`, and `google_workspace` flags,
- all merged ignore rules (`.gitignore`/`.graphifyignore`/CLI `--exclude`), and
- the file list — for extensions in `_PATH_DETERMINISTIC_EXTENSIONS` (code/paper/image, whose `FileType` is decided purely by path) only the path is hashed, but for everything else (extensionless shebang files, DOC/OFFICE/<COMPANY_NAME_REDACTED>-Workspace files) each file's `mtime_ns` + `size` is hashed too.

So adding/removing/renaming a file, changing ignore rules, toggling `follow_symlinks`/`google_workspace`, or editing the *content* of a non-path-deterministic file (e.g. a `.docx`) all invalidate it — but editing a code file's content does **not**, since code classification is path-only.

Artifacts: edited Dockerfile.coding-services
Result: `.detect_corpus_cache.json` caches the ~9-second corpus classification pass that sorts files into five categories. attributes.name: Graphify Incremental Rebuild — watch.py _rebuild_code
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Loads `.graphifyignore` rule files to determine which paths are excluded from corpus detection, extraction, and graph indexing. It is the single source of ignore semantics shared across all graphify subsystems.

## Architecture
- Core implementations live in `detect.py`, `extract.py`, and `watch.py` under `integrations/graphify/graphify/`
- Ignore rules loaded via `_load_graphifyignore` are merged and fed into `_corpus_signature` (in `detect.py`), so any change to `.graphifyignore` **invalidates the corpus detection cache** (`.detect_corpus_cache.json`)
- Referenced across ~14 files total: three core modules, their corresponding test files, shell scripts, changelog, and JSON export/config files — treat any single exact count as approximate

## Key Files
- `integrations/graphify/graphify/detect.py` — primary caller; merged ignore rules flow into corpus signature
- `integrations/graphify/graphify/extract.py` — uses ignore rules to skip files during extraction
- `integrations/graphify/graphify/watch.py` — uses ignore rules during file-watch incremental rebuild
- `integrations/graphify/tests/test_detect.py`, `test_extract.py`, `test_watch.py` — test coverage
- `scripts/graphify-reindex.sh` — shell-level caller
- `config/kgbench/questions/replication.json`, `docs/benchmarks/graphify-vs-grep/queries.json` — JSON configs referencing the function

## Usage
Called at the start of corpus detection, extraction, and watch-loop rebuild passes. The merged ignore ruleset is an input to `_corpus_signature`, meaning `.graphifyignore` changes propagate immediately to cache invalidation on the next run.

## Troubleshooting
- If files that should be ignored are included in the graph, verify `.graphifyignore` syntax and confirm `_load_graphifyignore` is being invoked in all three core modules
- If cache is not invalidating after ignore rule changes, confirm the merged rules are correctly passed into `_corpus_signature` in `detect.py`
- Delete `.detect_corpus_cache.json` to force a full re-detection

attributes.name: Graphify Incremental Rebuild — watch.py Call Chain
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Handles incremental rebuild operations within graphify's file-watch loop, re-running corpus detection and graph reconciliation when source files change — without requiring a full restart or full reindex.

## Architecture
- **`_rebuild_code`** (`integrations/graphify/graphify/watch.py`, line ~893): sole orchestrator of the incremental rebuild pipeline
- Calls `detect()` (from `detect.py`) at line ~1002 to recompute the corpus — hits `.detect_corpus_cache.json` if the SHA-256 signature is unchanged, saving ~9s of file classification work
- Calls **`_reconcile_existing_graph`** (also in `watch.py`, called exclusively by `_rebuild_code`) to update the in-memory/on-disk graph based on the newly detected corpus state
- Detection results feed directly into reconciliation; cache hits are transparent to this call site
- This is the **incremental path** — contrast with the full reindex triggered via `POST /api/cgr/reindex` → `graphify-reindex.sh`

## Key Files
- `integrations/graphify/graphify/watch.py` — contains `_rebuild_code` (~line 893), `detect()` call (~line 1002), and `_reconcile_existing_graph`
- `integrations/graphify/graphify/detect.py` — implements `detect()` and corpus caching logic
- `.detect_corpus_cache.json` — cache artifact; invalidated by corpus signature changes (including `.graphifyignore` edits)

## Usage
Triggered automatically by the file-watch loop when source files change. Not invoked directly; `_rebuild_code` is the entry point called by the watcher. The full reindex path (`POST /api/cgr/reindex`) bypasses this and uses `graphify-reindex.sh` instead.

## Troubleshooting
- **Stale graph after file changes**: check if `.detect_corpus_cache.json` is serving a stale hit; delete it to force full re-detection on the next watch event
- **`_reconcile_existing_graph` not reflecting changes**: confirm `detect()` returned an updated corpus — cache hit suppresses re-detection even if files changed if the signature (including ignore rules) is identical
- **`.graphifyignore` changes not taking effect**: any edit to `.graphifyignore` must invalidate the corpus signature; if not, delete the cache file manually

attributes.name: Intent: Understand why the benchmark harness removes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the
attributes.description:
Intent: Understand why the benchmark harness removes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the environment of spawned agents (this was a prior question being answered)
Approach: The assistant explained the security and control rationale: stripping the key forces agents through a local proxy rather than allowing direct API access, which preserves cost tracking, rate limiting, and routing controls on a shared billing account.
Artifacts: none
Result: The benchmark harness strips ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to prevent spawned agents from bypassing the local LLM proxy (llm-cli-proxy on port 12435) and hitting Anthropic's API directly, which would escape cost tracking and circuit-breaker controls. Without the key in the environment, headless `claude -p` subprocesses must route through the proxy instead of inheriting the corporate API key and connecting directly to Anthropic.

attributes.name: Containerizing Codegraph and Resolving Data Persistence Strategy
attributes.description:
The work session focused on migrating codegraph from a host-level dependency to a fully containerized setup (Phase 3), while also addressing data persistence across container rebuilds.

attributes.name: Benchmark Harness API Key Stripping Rationale Explained
attributes.description: Answered a standing question about why the benchmark harness removes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from spawned agent environments. Stripping the key forces headless `claude -p` subprocesses to route through the local LLM proxy (`llm-cli-proxy` on port `12435`) rather than connecting directly to Anthropic's API, preserving cost tracking, rate limiting, and circuit-breaker controls on the shared billing account. No files were modified.

attributes.description:
Intent: Understand why the benchmark harness strips ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the environment of spawned agents
Approach: The harness removes the API key to force all agents through the local rapid-llm-proxy for consistent routing, cost tracking, and billing; without this enforcement, agents would silently bypass the proxy and incur unbilled pay-per-token costs to Anthropic's API.
Artifacts: none
Result: The ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is stripped and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is pinned to the proxy (port 12435) to ensure every spawned agent uses measured, health-gated routing and centralized billing rather than direct API access, preventing spend leakage outside the proxy infrastructure.

attributes.name: Graphify Ignore Logic — _load_graphifyignore
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Loads `.graphifyignore` rule files to determine which paths are excluded from corpus detection, extraction, and graph indexing. It is the single source of ignore semantics shared across all graphify subsystems.

## Architecture
- Core implementations live in `detect.py`, `extract.py`, and `watch.py` under `integrations/graphify/graphify/`
- Ignore rules loaded via `_load_graphifyignore` are merged and fed into `_corpus_signature` (in `detect.py`), so any change to `.graphifyignore` **invalidates the corpus detection cache** (`.detect_corpus_cache.json`)
- Referenced across ~14 files total: three core modules, their corresponding test files, shell scripts, changelog, and JSON export/config files — treat any single exact count as approximate

## Key Files
- `integrations/graphify/graphify/detect.py` — primary caller; merged ignore rules flow into corpus signature
- `integrations/graphify/graphify/extract.py` — uses ignore rules to skip files during extraction
- `integrations/graphify/graphify/watch.py` — uses ignore rules during file-watch incremental rebuild
- `integrations/graphify/tests/test_detect.py`, `test_extract.py`, `test_watch.py` — test coverage
- `scripts/graphify-reindex.sh` — shell-level caller
- `config/kgbench/questions/replication.json`, `docs/benchmarks/graphify-vs-grep/queries.json` — JSON configs referencing the function

## Usage
Called at the start of corpus detection, extraction, and watch-loop rebuild passes. The merged ignore ruleset is an input to `_corpus_signature`, meaning `.graphifyignore` changes propagate immediately to cache invalidation on the next run.

## Troubleshooting
- If files that should be ignored are included in the graph, verify `.graphifyignore` syntax and confirm `_load_graphifyignore` is being invoked in all three core modules
- If cache is not invalidating after ignore rule changes, confirm the merged rules are correctly passed into `_corpus_signature` in `detect.py`
- Delete `.detect_corpus_cache.json` to force a full re-detection

attributes.name: Intent: Understand why the benchmark harness removes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from spaw
attributes.description:
Intent: Understand why the benchmark harness removes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from spawned agent environments
Approach: The harness strips the key to enforce routing discipline — without it, subprocess agents would connect directly to Anthropic's API (via environment or .env), bypassing cost tracking, usage metering, and subscription routing through the local proxy, causing billing inconsistencies and potential failures when raw API credits are exhausted.
Artifacts: none
Result: The harness enforces all benchmark agent traffic through a local proxy (`:12435`) by stripping ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and requiring explicit `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` configuration, ensuring consistent measurement, billing, and Claude Max subscription routing instead of silent direct API leakage.

Answer in 2-3 sentences.","createdAt":"2026-08-05T19:38:32.640Z","metadata":{"agent":"claude","format":"live"}},{"id":"9dd8fa08-65f4-410a-b49c-5baf584021d1-assistant","role":"assistant","content":"Because a headless `claude -p` subprocess spawned by the harness will pick up `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the environment (e.g. via `.env`) if it's present, and that causes it to talk directly to Anthropic's API instead of going through the local proxy — bypassing both the cost/usage tracking and the Claude Max subscription routing (leading to errors like "Credit balance too low" once the raw API key's credits are exhausted).

Stripping the key forces the subprocess to fail closed unless `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is pinned to the proxy (`:12435`), which is the desired behavior — all benchmark-agent traffic must route through the proxy so it's measured and billed consistently rather than silently leaking to direct API access.

attributes.name: Intent: Fix two defects in the coding-v1 question set harness before running the
attributes.description:
Intent: Fix two defects in the coding-v1 question set harness before running the full experiment — move ground truth out of the searchable tree to prevent test contamination, and refine the forbidden matcher to distinguish asserting a location from merely mentioning one.
Approach: The solution isolates the question set from arms' search scope (eliminating accidental answer-key reads) and makes the hallucination grader context-aware (distinguishing claimed locations from incidental path mentions in explanations). This prevents false contamination signals and false hallucination flags that nearly produced an invalid benchmark result on the pilot run.
Artifacts: none
Result: Two critical defects were identified and scoped for fixing before the full coding-v1 experiment runs. Test contamination occurred because questions lived in the searchable repo and grep read the answer key; false hallucination flagging fired on any path-shaped string, including paths mentioned during explanation. The pilot's headline result is invalidated but was caught by the harness's own verification machinery — the exact scenario it was designed to prevent. Branch has nine commits staged; fixes are required before proceeding to full experiment execution.

metadata.messages:
[{"id":"0053ffb3-ef95-43e4-b06a-b3499c6b6932-user","role":"user","content":"All three items are done, but the question set needs one more pass before it can produce trustworthy numbers.

install.sh + docs — done (ea1709453)

_install_codegraph_support() creates the two things Docker and agents can't create themselves: the .codegraph/ mountpoint (Docker can't mkdir under a read-only parent — miss it and the container won't start) and .data/codegraph/. It warns if a real codegraph binary is on PATH, detected by content (does it delegate to docker exec?) rather than path — a path comparison false-positived on our own shim during testing. Docs page written, mirrored into docs-content/, added to the nav.

.data persistence — done (88c875d3a)

Rebuild-safety already held via the bind mount, but by accident of two compose mounts and a tracked empty dir. Ten tests now pin them so tidying can't silently break it. Provenance is committed (gate results, sidecars, run summaries, question sets, reports); indexes stay out.

One thing that bit me: codegraph writes its own .gitignore containing * into .data/codegraph, which silently overrode my root-level negations — the artifacts looked tracked and weren't. Sidecars now live in .data/code-graph-<COMPANY_NAME_REDACTED>/, which no backend manages.

Question set — 17 questions, and a pilot I'm glad I ran

coding-v1 is first-party-only, multi-hop, with a new abstain class. The provenance verifier machine-checks all 27 file:line references and is wired into test-coding.sh.

The 3-arm pilot confirmed it discriminates where the replication set didn't — but it also exposed two defects in my own set, and they invalidate the pilot's headline result:

1. Test contamination. The questions live in the repo the arms search. grep's answer to T3 literally began "This question is a known abstain probe from config/kgbench/questions/coding-v1.json" — it read the answer key. Any arm with file access can.

The guide covers tool-specific workflows for `semantic-analysis_generate_plantuml_diagrams` and `semantic-analysis_create_insight_report`, with clear examples of correct vs. incorrect patterns.

Artifacts: none

Result: A centralized, enforced documentation style guide now governs all artifact creation and modification across the project, reducing inconsistency violations, preventing orphaned files, ensuring PlantUML diagrams use the standard style, and establishing clear workflows for generating and placing diagrams. metadata.messages:
[{"id":"f84c2937-4d4f-4b3d-8436-993976cb521b-user","role":"user","content":"# Documentation Style Guide

Enforce consistent styling for documentation artifacts (PlantUML, Mermaid, markdown, PNG diagrams).

## Instructions

When creating or modifying documentation artifacts, follow these guidelines strictly.

---

## HARD RULES — File Placement (Constraint-Monitored)

These rules are enforced by the constraint monitor. Violations trigger system health degradation.

| Artifact | MUST be placed in | NEVER place in |
|----------|-------------------|----------------|
| `.puml` files | `docs/puml/` | Root, `src/`, temp dirs, or anywhere else |
| Generated `.png` | `docs/images/` | Same dir as `.puml`, root, or temp dirs |
| Image references in markdown | `![alt](docs/images/file.png)` | `![alt](./file.png)` or absolute paths |

**When using tools that generate diagrams** (e.g., `semantic-analysis_generate_plantuml_diagrams`, `create_insight_report`):
- Always specify output paths pointing to `docs/puml/` for `.puml` files
- Always specify `docs/images/` for rendered PNG output
- Use the `name` parameter as kebab-case without path — the tool writes to CWD, so run from `docs/puml/` or move files after generation
- If a tool does NOT support specifying output directory, move the generated files immediately after creation

**`semantic-analysis_generate_plantuml_diagrams` specific workflow:**
1. Call the tool with `name` set to a kebab-case descriptor (e.g., `"constraint-monitor-architecture"`)
2. After generation, immediately move output: `mv *.puml docs/puml/ && mv *.png docs/images/`
3. Verify the generated `.puml` contains `!include _standard-style.puml` — add it if missing
4. Update any markdown references to point to `docs/images/`

**`semantic-analysis_create_insight_report` specific workflow:**
- Insight reports with diagrams write to `.sa/insights/` by default — this is fine for internal analysis
- If diagrams from insights need to be committed to docs, copy them to `docs/puml/` and `docs/images/`

**PlantUML file naming** — MUST use `component-purpose.puml` kebab-case convention:
- `constraint-monitor-architecture.puml` ✓
- `ConstraintMonitorArchitecture.puml` ✗
- `diagram-v2.puml` ✗ (incremental naming forbidden)

---

## PlantUML Diagrams (.puml)

### File Naming Convention

**CRITICAL**: Use kebab-case, descriptive names. NEVER use incremental suffixes.

**Correct**:
- `health-verification-flow.puml`
- `knowledge-architecture.puml`
- `constraint-monitor-components.puml`

**WRONG** (constraint violation):
- `health-verification-flow-2.puml`
- `knowledge-architecture-v2.puml`
- `constraint-monitor-components-new.puml`

If updating an existing diagram, **modify the existing file** rather than creating a new version.

### Standard Style Include

All PlantUML files MUST include the standard style at the top:

```plantuml
@startuml diagram-name
!include _standard-style.puml

' ... diagram content ...

@enduml
```

The style file is located at:
- `docs/puml/_standard-style.puml`
- `docs/presentation/puml/_standard-style.puml`

### Layout Guidelines

1. **Prefer vertical layouts** - Avoid excessive width that requires horizontal scrolling
2. **Use `top to bottom direction`** for most diagrams
3. **Use `left to right direction`** only for sequence diagrams or when horizontal flow is semantically meaningful
4. **Group related components** using packages or rectangles

### Component Stereotypes

Use these stereotypes for consistent coloring:

| Stereotype | Color | Use For |
|------------|-------|---------|
| `<<api>>` | Light Blue | API endpoints, REST interfaces |
| `<<core>>` | Light Green | Core business logic |
| `<<storage>>` | Light Yellow | Databases, file storage |
| `<<cli>>` | Light Pink | Command-line interfaces |
| `<<util>>` | Light Gray | Utility/helper components |
| `<<agent>>` | Soft Blue | AI agents, autonomous components |
| `<<infra>>` | Light <COMPANY_NAME_REDACTED> | Infrastructure components |
| `<<external>>` | Neutral Gray | External systems |

### Arrow Macros

Use defined macros for consistent arrow styling:

```plantuml
SYNC_LINE     ' Red solid line - synchronous calls
ASYNC_LINE    ' Green dashed - async/event-based
DATA_LINE     ' <COMPANY_NAME_REDACTED> solid - data flow
CONTROL_LINE  ' Purple solid - control flow
OPTIONAL_LINE ' Gray dotted - optional paths
```

---

## PNG Generation

### Generating PNGs from PlantUML

Use the `plantuml` command-line tool (installed via Homebrew):

```bash
# Local generation using plantuml CLI (preferred)
plantuml -tpng docs/puml/diagram-name.puml -o ../images/

# Generate all diagrams in a directory
plantuml -tpng docs/puml/*.puml -o ../images/

# Or use the docs script if available
./scripts/generate-diagrams.sh
```

**Note:** The `plantuml` CLI is installed via `brew install plantuml` and handles Java dependencies automatically.

### PNG Naming

PNG files should match their source PUML file:
- `health-verification-flow.puml` → `health-verification-flow.png`

### Output Location

PNGs should be generated to:
- `docs/images/` - For markdown documentation references
- `docs/presentation/images/` - For presentation diagrams

---

## Mermaid Diagrams

### Inline in Markdown

Use fenced code blocks with `mermaid` language:

```markdown
```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Start] --> B{Decision}
    B -->|Yes| C[Action]
    B -->|No| D[End]
```
```

### Style Guidelines

1. Use clear, descriptive node labels
2. Keep diagrams focused - split large diagrams into multiple
3. Use subgraphs for logical grouping
4. Prefer `graph TD` (top-down) over `graph LR` (left-right) for readability

---

## Markdown Documentation

### File Naming

- Use kebab-case: `api-quota-checker.md`
- Use `README.md` for directory index files
- Never use spaces or special characters

### Structure

1. Start with H1 title matching the topic
2. Include brief overview paragraph
3. Use H2 for major sections
4. Use H3 for subsections
5. Include code examples where applicable

### Links

- Use relative paths for internal links: `[Status Line](./status-line.md)`
- Use absolute URLs for external links
- Verify links work before committing

---

## Validation Workflow

Before committing documentation changes:

1. **PlantUML**: Verify syntax by generating PNG
2. **Mermaid**: Preview in VS Code or GitHub
3. **Markdown**: Check rendering in preview
4. **Links**: Verify all internal links work
5. **Images**: Ensure referenced images exist

---

## Common Violations to Avoid

1. **Incremental naming** (`-2`, `-v2`, `-new` suffixes)
2. **Missing style include** in PlantUML
3. **Horizontal-heavy layouts** causing scroll
4. **Orphaned images** (PNG without source PUML)
5. **Broken internal links**
6. **Inconsistent component colors** (not using stereotypes)

---

## Quick Reference

| Artifact | Location | Naming | Style |
|----------|----------|--------|-------|
| PlantUML | `docs/puml/` | kebab-case.puml | Include `_standard-style.puml` |
| PNG | `docs/images/` | match-source.png | Generated from PUML |
| Markdown | `docs/*/` | kebab-case.md | H1 title, H2 sections |
| Mermaid | Inline | N/A | graph TD preferred |

attributes.name: Intent: Understand what coding-v1 is in the context of the kgbench evaluation fr
attributes.description:
Intent: Understand what coding-v1 is in the context of the kgbench evaluation framework
Approach: Provided a comprehensive explanation of coding-v1 as the question set for the benchmark, detailing its design philosophy (first-party evidence, multi-hop synthesis, abstain class), composition (16 active questions across 5 classes), and scoring methodology (facts_found/facts_required with hallucination detection via forbidden facts). Contextualized this by explaining T2's retirement due to a false premise (answer lived in a submodule despite first-party-only design), and how that decision is now explicitly recorded in the config rather than silently omitted.
Artifacts: edited runner.mjs, edited kgbench-tool-enforcement.test.js
Result: coding-v1 is a 16-question evaluation set designed to discriminate between code understanding approaches by requiring multi-hop reasoning and penalizing confident hallucination via an abstain class; it replaces the earlier replication set which suffered from inability to discriminate. T2 (1 of 17 original questions) was retired with evidence recorded inline, and the benchmark is running 144 test cells (16 questions × 3 arms × 3 reps) with machine-verified ground truth references.

metadata.messages:
[{"id":"queued_2026-08-05T21:22:54.807Z-user","role":"user","content":"what is coding-v1?","createdAt":"2026-08-05T21:22:54.807Z","metadata":{"agent":"claude","format":"live"}},{"id":"queued_2026-08-05T21:22:54.807Z-assistant","role":"assistant","content":"[Tool calls]
Bash: git add config/kgbench/questions/coding-v1.json lib/kgbench/arms.mjs lib/kgbench/report.mjs scripts/kgbench-report.mjs &

**`coding-v1` is the question set** — the evaluation data the benchmark runs, as opposed to the harness that runs it. It lives at `config/kgbench/questions/coding-v1.json`.

It replaced the earlier `replication` set, which couldn't discriminate: both arms scored 1.00 on every class. (We now know a large part of why — the arms weren't actually isolated, so "both arms" were the same agent.)

Three deliberate design choices, per the set's own header:

1. **First-party evidence only.** No question cites a submodule, because CI runs with `submodules: false`, and questions about graphify's internals would become meaningless if graphify were swapped out — which is the decision this benchmark exists to inform. (Ironically, T2's *answer* turned out to live in a submodule, which is exactly how its false premise slipped through.)
2. **Multi-hop and synthesis.** The replication questions mostly resolved with one well-chosen grep, which is why grep tied everywhere. These require joining facts across files, or narrative that isn't in any single location.
3. **An abstain class.** Questions whose answer is *not* in the repo, including two about code genuinely removed (code-graph-rag / Memgraph). A stale index answers those confidently and wrongly; grep comes up empty. That asymmetry is the most decision-relevant thing a benchmark can surface, and correctness-only scoring hides it.

Composition after retiring T2 — **16 active questions**:

| Class | n | What it tests |
|---|--:|---|
| `lookup` | 3 | Single-fact retrieval (e.g. which file defines `MANAGED_MCP_KEYS`) |
| `structural` | 3 | Relationships between code elements |
| `blast` | 3 | Blast radius — what breaks if X changes |
| `arch` | 4 | Narrative/architectural synthesis |
| `abstain` | 3 | The answer isn't here; saying so is the only correct response |

Scoring is `facts_found / facts_required` against a per-question `checklist`; any `forbidden` fact forces 0 and flags hallucination. Every `provenance.evidence` entry is a `file:line` reference machine-checked by `scripts/kgbench-verify-questions.mjs` (27 references, all resolving), so the ground truth can't rot silently.

---

**T2 is now retired** — `enabled: false`, kept in the file rather than deleted, with the evidence recorded inline:

> `cgr-query-cache.ts:233` constructs `MATCH (e)-[:CALLS]->(callee) ... RETURN DISTINCT callee.name`. Arms that produced that query were RIGHT and scored 0; the arm that abstained scored 1.

I retired it for a **false premise, not for scoring badly** — that distinction is written into the file, since dropping questions because results look wrong is selection. The report now names excluded questions explicitly rather than quietly omitting them. The verifier still checks all 17 (including the retired one), so its evidence can't rot either.

16 questions × 3 arms × 3 reps = 144 cells. The run is in flight; I'll bring you the results when it lands.
","createdAt":"2026-08-05T21:22:54.807Z","metadata":{"agent":"claude","format":"live"}}]

attributes.name: coding-v1 Benchmark — Design and Scoring
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Cross-agent matrix runs (`coding-v1-x1`, `coding-v1-x2`) execute a 384-cell benchmark grid across multiple agents (Claude, Copilot, opencode) and retrieval arms (grep, graphify, codegraph, hybrid) to measure per-agent tool preference and retrieval quality.

## Architecture
- **Matrix size**: 384 cells — agents × arms × questions × replicates
- **Resume/done-set keying**: completed cells are tracked in a done-set; `api_error` cells are written to the done-set and skipped on resume — this is a known design gap for retryable errors (e.g. session-limit errors)
- **Failure taxonomy**: `api_error`, `HOST_STALLED`, `TOOL_ESCAPE`, `CONTAM`; `api_error` cells must be manually deleted from the done-set and re-run to restore balanced class median coverage
- **Hybrid arm**: present in config; produces data under `hybrid/claude` arm label; observed to be active in x2 run (38 cells analyzed)
- **Tool-preference finding** (replicated across x1 and x2): agents with both text-search and graph tools strongly prefer text-search — `hybrid/claude` arm shows ~114 `Grep` calls vs. ~3 graph-tool calls; graph tools score 1.00 when forced but are rarely chosen voluntarily
- **Post-run repair sequence**: (1) backfill late token writes from Copilot/opencode stop-adapters, (2) delete and re-run failed `api_error` cells, (3) backfill again, (4) generate final per-agent report covering tool-choice, token provenance, and graph-vs-grep comparison
- **Run monitoring**: `supervise.log` records abort reason and cell count; distinguish intentional abort from crash before resuming

## Key Files
- `supervise.log` — run progress and abort records; inspect before resuming a partial run
- `config/kgbench/arms.json` — arm definitions including hybrid arm
- `lib/kgbench/arms.mjs` — arm loading and `argvForAgent` helper
- `kgbench-run.mjs` — benchmark entry point

## Usage

## Purpose
Cross-agent matrix runs (`coding-v1-x1`, `coding-v1-x2`) execute a 384-cell benchmark grid across multiple agents (Claude, Copilot, opencode) and retrieval arms (grep, graphify, codegraph, hybrid) to measure per-agent tool preference and retrieval quality.

## Architecture
- **Matrix size**: 384 cells — agents × arms × questions × replicates
- **Resume/done-set keying**: completed cells are tracked in a done-set; `api_error` cells are written to the done-set and skipped on resume — this is a known design gap for retryable errors (e.g. session-limit errors)
- **Failure taxonomy**: `api_error`, `HOST_STALLED`, `TOOL_ESCAPE`, `CONTAM`; `api_error` cells must be manually deleted from the done-set and re-run to restore balanced class median coverage
- **Hybrid arm**: present in config; produces data under `hybrid/claude` arm label; observed to be active in x2 run (38 cells analyzed)
- **Tool-preference finding** (replicated across x1 and x2): agents with both text-search and graph tools strongly prefer text-search — `hybrid/claude` arm shows ~114 `Grep` calls vs. ~3 graph-tool calls; graph tools score 1.00 when forced but are rarely chosen voluntarily
- **Post-run repair sequence**: (1) backfill late token writes from Copilot/opencode stop-adapters, (2) delete and re-run failed `api_error` cells, (3) backfill again, (4) generate final per-agent report covering tool-choice, token provenance, and graph-vs-grep comparison
- **Run monitoring**: `supervise.log` records abort reason and cell count; distinguish intentional abort from crash before resuming

attributes.name: coding-v1 Benchmark — results.jsonl Polling and CONTAM Detection
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Guards benchmark integrity by flagging cells where an agent may have accessed ground-truth data outside the permitted retrieval path. A known design flaw causes false positives that void legitimate scores.

## Architecture
- **Signal classification design flaw**: The detector conflates inference-based reasoning artifacts (agent citing/quoting a test case in its explanation) with genuine data leakage. Not all signals should trigger score voidance.
- **Known false positive class — mention-vs-assert**: fires when an agent *mentions* benchmark data in its reasoning even when it did not assert privileged knowledge. Reasoning artifacts must be separated from genuine contamination signals.
- **Confirmed affected test cases**: graphify arm (confirmed false positive during clean-run event processing); grep arm T3 rep2 (`coding-v1-isolated` run) — sandbox isolation was in place, making a genuine escape unlikely; raw answer content must be inspected to distinguish mention-vs-assert from real leakage.
- **Diagnosis procedure**: inspect the raw answer content from the flagged `results.jsonl` row to determine whether the agent quoted/cited benchmark data in reasoning vs. asserted privileged knowledge it could not have retrieved legitimately.
- **Remediation direction**: full signal handling architecture refactor required; patching individual regex patterns is insufficient and was explicitly rejected. No files have been modified yet.

## Key Files
- `results.jsonl` — append-only output; flagged rows contain the raw answer content needed for CONTAM diagnosis
- Contamination detector (location TBD pending refactor) — conflates mention with assertion

## Usage
CONTAM flags appear in `results.jsonl` cells. Each flag requires manual triage: retrieve the raw answer from the flagged row and determine whether the agent cited data (mention) or demonstrated knowledge it could only have obtained via leakage (assert). Sandbox isolation reduces but does not eliminate the need for this check.

## Troubleshooting
- **CONTAM on a sandboxed arm**: first hypothesis is mention-vs-assert false positive. Read the raw answer text from the flagged row in `results.jsonl` before voiding the cell.
- **Cannot distinguish mention vs. assert from summary fields**: full raw body capture must be enabled; see Raw-Body Capture Pipeline insight.
- **Recurring false positives on the same question**: indicates the trap phrase or ground-truth text appears in agent reasoning templates; requires signal architecture refactor, not regex patching.

attributes.name: Intent: Verify and investigate why T2 questions were scoring zeros in the kgbenc
attributes.description:
Intent: Verify and investigate why T2 questions were scoring zeros in the kgbench run, checking the actual data and question definitions.

Approach: The developer discovered that T2 zeros were not a grader artifact but exposed a cascade of deeper issues: the `--allowedTools` restriction was not enforcing tool isolation (both arms used identical tool surfaces including Bash despite different grants), arms mutated the sandbox worktree by running `git submodule update`, and T2's ground truth incorrectly assumed a function no longer existed when it actually does exist as a shim. The fix involved implementing proper post-hoc enforcement via `--disallowedTools` (which *is* enforced even under skip-permissions) and a cell-voiding mechanism that counts only executed tool calls, not attempted ones, to prevent false positives from denied requests.

Artifacts: edited /Users/<USER_ID_REDACTED>/Agentic/coding/lib/kgbench/runner.mjs, edited /Users/<USER_ID_REDACTED>/Agentic/coding/tests/integration/kgbench-tool-enforcement.test.js

Result: Tool enforcement is now correctly implemented: denied tools are excluded from the model's schema surface, denied tool calls are refused by the model, and any cell where an ungranted tool was actually executed is marked `tool_escape` and excluded from scoring. The run restarted with 58 passing tests and baseline token usage dropped from 67,459 to 48,146, confirming the tool surface changed. T2's ground truth remains flagged as incorrect (the queried function exists as a shim) but scoring is left as-is pending developer decision on reclassification or removal.

These are not grader artefacts — they look like a **question defect**. But two of the claims are suspicious (no arm has Bash, yet rep2 claims it ran `git submodule update --init`). Let me verify against the real repo:
`runCypherQuery` genuinely exists — in a **submodule**. The critical question is whether the sandbox worktree contains it, or whether an arm read outside the sandbox:
The submodule was populated at 22:59 — *after* the tree was built at 22:31. That means containment may have been verified on an incomplete tree. Investigating:
This is worse than a question defect. Look at the tools the arms actually used:

- **grep arm**: `Bash` × 59, plus `Agent`, `SendMessage`, `TaskStop` — none of which are in its `allowedTools`
- **graphify arm**: `Bash` × 27, `Read` × 4 — and **not one graphify MCP tool**

`--allowedTools` is not restricting anything. Stopping the run — it is measuring nothing:
Let me confirm the exact mechanism directly rather than infer it:
`--disallowedTools` enforces even under `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Let me confirm the allowlist-only case actually *executes* (not merely attempts), so my claim is exact:
My own sandbox blocked that test (correctly). I already have conclusive evidence from the run itself — let me confirm the arm read *real* content rather than hallucinating:
Fully established. The arm's quoted Cypher matches `cgr-query-cache.ts:233` character-for-character — it really read the file, inside the sandbox, from a submodule that `git worktree add` leaves empty. It ran `git submodule update` via Bash.

Let me fix the enforcement:
Now the verification half — a cell whose arm used an ungranted tool must not be scorable:
Now a live end-to-end check that enforcement actually holds:
Bash is denied. But this exposes a trap in my own fix: the denied call still appears in `tools`, so a *refused* attempt would falsely void the cell. I need to count only tools that actually executed:
Both correct — no false voiding, and `Grep` correctly recorded as executed. Adding regression tests, then restarting:
Baselines dropped from 67,459 → 48,146 tokens — direct confirmation the tool surface actually changed (denied tools' schemas are no longer loaded). Monitoring:
You were right to have me check the T2 zeros now. They weren't a grader artefact — they exposed something that invalidates the whole matrix.

## The T2 zeros are a question defect sitting on top of a harness defect

The immediate finding: **T2's ground truth is wrong.** It assumes `runCypherQuery` no longer exists. It does exist — in `integrations/mcp-server-semantic-analysis`, as a "best-effort Cypher shim over graph.json", with literal Cypher strings in `cgr-query-cache.ts`. The arms that scored 0 gave *more accurate* answers than the one that scored 1.

But two claims in those answers didn't add up. One said it ran `git submodule update --init` — and no arm has Bash. That's what I pulled on.

## The arms were never isolated

`--allowedTools` is a permission-*prompt* allowlist. `--dangerously-skip-permissions` skips consulting it. So every arm got the full default tool surface:

| Arm | Tools actually used |
|---|---|
| grep | `Grep`×144, **`Bash`×59**, `Read`×38, `Glob`×4, **`Agent`**×2, `SendMessage`, `TaskStop` |
| graphify | **`Bash`×27**, `Read`×4 — **not one graphify MCP tool** |

Both arms were the same agent wearing different labels. Nothing about retrieval strategy was being measured.

**This retrospectively explains the replication run.** Both arms scored 1.00 on every class and "could not tell the arms apart" — read at the time as the questions being too easy. The likelier reason is that the arms were identical.

It also breached the sandbox I'd just built. An arm ran `git submodule update --init` *inside* the worktree, checking out a submodule that `git worktree add` leaves empty, then answered T2 from it — quoting `cgr-query-cache.ts:233` character-for-character, which I verified against the real file. Containment was verified at 22:31; the arm mutated the tree at 22:59. **Verifying once at setup isn't enough when the arm can write.**

## Fix, in both halves

`--disallowedTools` (built-ins minus the arm's grant) *is* enforced under skip-permissions — verified live: the model tries Bash and is told it's "disabled entirely, including for subagents."

The guarantee is the post-hoc check: a cell whose arm **executed** an ungranted tool becomes `tool_escape` and cannot be scored. Executed, not attempted — a denied tool still emits a `tool_use` block, so counting attempts would have voided nearly every cell. While monitoring the in-progress benchmark run (40/153 cells, ~50 min remaining), a contamination event was detected: the grep arm was finding abstain probe trap phrases quoted verbatim inside comments in `sandbox.mjs` and `graders.mjs`.

- Sanitized offending comments and added a WARNING documenting the authoring rule prohibiting verbatim trap phrase quotes
- Implemented `leak_terms` declaration mechanism on questions for decisive must-not-appear strings
- Added an invariant in `createRunTree` verifying exclusion globs cannot delete question evidence files
- Modified `sandbox.mjs`; clean run restarted with all three arms baselined at ~48k tokens each (~55 min expected)

attributes.name: KGBench Timeout Handling and Circuit-Breaker Under Host Contention
attributes.description:
A monitoring notification surfaced a timeout failure on the grep task (B1, rep1, 948s), which was diagnosed as Node.js event loop starvation caused by corporate security software (Defender, epsext, CyberArk, Nexthink) saturating CPU to 201% — causing the 300s timeout to fire at wall-clock ~950s.

- Distinguished `host_stalled` events from genuine timeouts; `host_stalled` excluded from `RETRYABLE_ERRORS` to prevent wasteful retry loops burning ~950s each
- Increased `timeoutMs` from 300,000ms → 600,000ms to reflect realistic latency under host contention
- Added circuit-breaker logic in `runner.mjs` to halt execution early when an arm is consistently timing out under the same host conditions
- Also modified `kgbench-run.mjs`
